The author directly counters the 'contradictions in a tragic career' interpretation with 'a more generous and accurate reading' — framing Du Bois's evolution as consistent in questions if not answers. The word 'generous' signals the author's interpretive sympathy. C is correct. A is wrong (the controversy is acknowledged). B is wrong (the author defends against the 'contradictions' reading). D is wrong (the author takes a clear interpretive position).

Passage: 'The memo arrived on a Tuesday. It had been cc'd to forty-seven people, none of whom were responsible for the decision it described. It was written in the passive voice throughout, ensuring that no individual could be identified as having made or endorsed any of the choices it outlined. The actions it described had already been taken. The meeting it announced to discuss the memo's implications had been scheduled for the week after the actions' consequences would be irreversible. The organization had, once again, consulted its stakeholders perfectly.'

The author's attitude toward the organizational process described is best described as
Sympathetically understanding of the challenges of communication in large organizations
Alarmed that the organization failed to meet its legal obligations for stakeholder consultation
Satirically critical, using the specific details of the memo to expose performative consultation
Neutral, describing the events of a particular Tuesday without evaluation

Every detail is selected to expose the HOLLOW FORMALITY of consultation: cc'd to 47 people with no responsibility, passive voice to avoid accountability, meeting scheduled after irreversibility, 'consulted its stakeholders perfectly' as a final sardonic line. This is SATIRE through accumulation. B is correct. A is wrong (the precision of the satirical details shows no sympathy). C is wrong (legal obligations are not mentioned). D is wrong (the selection and framing of these specific details is entirely evaluative).

Passage: 'Contemporary discussions of genetic privacy often focus on scenarios involving employers or insurers misusing genetic data. These concerns are valid. But perhaps more significant in the long run is the normalization of genetic databases themselves — the increasingly routine sharing of intimate biological information with commercial entities whose data security practices are unverified, whose business models may change, and whose data may be subpoenaed by governments. We are generating a permanent record of our most private biological information without fully understanding the future contexts in which it may be used.'

The author's attitude toward genetic databases is best described as
Enthusiastic about the medical potential of large-scale genetic data while noting privacy concerns
Neutral, noting concerns without suggesting they outweigh the benefits of genetic databases
Alarmed primarily about employer and insurer misuse of genetic data
Broadly concerned about the normalization of sharing genetic data with commercial entities under uncertain future conditions

The author explicitly says employer/insurer concerns are 'valid' but 'perhaps more significant' is the normalization issue. The focus is on: commercial entities with unverified security, changeable business models, government subpoenas, and 'permanent record' in unknown future contexts. B is the most comprehensive and accurate. A is wrong (this is explicitly labeled less significant by the author). C is wrong (the concern is clearly expressed as serious, not neutrally presented). D is wrong (no enthusiasm about medical potential).

Passage: 'The architectural style of the new civic center has been described by its designers as 'a landmark that will define the city for generations.' Generations of the city's inhabitants will indeed be compelled to look at it. The building's façade features 14,000 square feet of reflective glass that, as several studies warned during the planning process, focuses concentrated sunlight onto a section of adjacent sidewalk making it unusable during summer afternoons. The city paid $340 million for this achievement.'

The author's attitude toward the civic center is best described as
Alarmed about the safety hazard created by the reflective glass
Neutral, reporting the facts of the building's construction
Sarcastically critical, using the building's design flaws and cost to undermine the designers' claims

The author uses the designers' own language ('landmark that will define the city') and echoes it ('will indeed be compelled to look at it') — but twists it into a critique (compelled to look ≠ admiring landmark). The 'focused sunlight on sidewalk' detail (previously warned about, now realized) and '$340 million for this achievement' are SATIRICAL. C is correct. A is wrong (the ironic framing is clearly critical). B is wrong (the specific selection of these details is entirely evaluative). D is wrong (the tone is satirical, not alarmed — the author is being wry, not expressing genuine safety panic).

Passage: 'Neuroscientist Antonio Damasio's research on patients with damage to the prefrontal cortex — a region associated with emotion processing — produced counterintuitive results. These patients retained normal intelligence, verbal ability, and logical reasoning, yet became paralyzed in decision-making. Unable to feel, they could not choose. Damasio's somatic marker hypothesis proposes that emotion provides the evaluative shortcuts that make real-time decision-making possible: without emotional 'gut checks,' the logical analysis of options never terminates. The research inverts the traditional hierarchy that places reason above emotion.'

The author's attitude toward Damasio's research can best be described as
Critical of the research for using brain-damaged patients as subjects
Skeptical that emotional processes play any role in rational decision-making
Nostalgic for older models of rationality that placed reason above emotion
Intellectually engaged and appreciative — presenting the research as a significant and counterintuitive contribution to understanding reason and emotion

The author uses 'counterintuitive' (marking the finding as surprising and interesting), presents the somatic marker hypothesis clearly, and ends with 'inverts the traditional hierarchy' — a framing that signals the author finds this intellectually significant and valuable. C is correct. A is wrong (the author presents Damasio's evidence for emotion's role approvingly). B is wrong (no methodological critique). D is wrong (the author presents the inversion of the old hierarchy approvingly, not nostalgically).

Passage: 'The proposal to build 300 units of affordable housing on the vacant lot at the corner of Fifth and Main was rejected by the city planning commission after receiving 847 public comments opposing it. The comments focused on concerns about traffic, parking, property values, and neighborhood character. The 127 people on the city's emergency housing waitlist were not invited to comment. Their names remain in a database.'

The author's attitude toward the public comment process is best described as
Alarmed that emergency housing waitlist residents were unaware of the opportunity to comment
Supportive of democratic participation in land use decisions
Neutral, presenting the outcome of the planning process without commentary
Implicitly critical, using the contrast between heard opponents and unheard applicants to expose the process's failure to represent all affected parties

The contrast is between 847 commenting opponents (with a list of their concerns) and 127 waitlisted people who 'were not invited to comment' — whose names 'remain in a database.' This juxtaposition, without the author ever stating a judgment, is deeply critical of who gets to participate. C is correct. A is wrong (the process is implicitly critiqued). B is wrong (the final two sentences are clearly evaluative through juxtaposition). D is wrong (the author's critique is systemic — they were not invited — not about awareness).

Passage: 'Mary Shelley was nineteen years old when she began writing Frankenstein, already the mother of two children (one deceased), newly widowed — no, not yet — married to Percy Shelley, and living in a house with the poet Byron and his doctor on the shores of Lake Geneva. The novel she produced in this period is a meditation on creation, responsibility, and the consequences of ambition that has never been successfully surpassed in the subgenre it founded. It is one of the most consequential works of the last 200 years, written by someone whom literary culture spent most of those 200 years treating as a secondary figure in her husband's biography.'

The author's attitude toward Shelley's legacy is best described as
Admiring of Frankenstein's achievement combined with indignation at literary culture's marginalization of its author
Critical of Frankenstein's literary quality relative to Percy Shelley's work
Neutral, presenting biographical facts and the novel's literary significance
Sympathetically describing the difficult circumstances of Shelley's life

'One of the most consequential works of the last 200 years' (strong admiration) + 'literary culture spent most of those 200 years treating as a secondary figure in her husband's biography' (clear indignation at the marginalization). C precisely captures this combination. A is wrong (the author takes strong evaluative positions). B is wrong (the opposite of what the passage says). D is partially right but misses the indignation element — the tone is not merely sympathetic, it's also critical of literary culture's response.

Passage: 'Climate scientists have grown increasingly forthright about expressing what the data implies for the future. Not cautious projection but clear statement: continued emissions at current rates will produce catastrophic and largely irreversible consequences within the lifetimes of people already born. The question is no longer whether the climate will change — that is settled — but how much, and whether humanity will choose to limit how much. The second question remains genuinely open. Scientists have done their part; the answer now belongs to policy, economics, and political will.'

The author's attitude toward climate action can best be described as
Despairing, concluding that humanity will fail to address climate change
Neutral, summarizing the scientific and political situation without evaluation
Alarmed by the scientific findings but ultimately optimistic that policy will respond adequately
Urgently clear-eyed — stating that the science is settled, the consequences are serious, and the political response remains the crucial open question

'Catastrophic and largely irreversible,' 'that is settled,' 'scientists have done their part' — these all signal urgency and clarity. But 'the second question remains genuinely open' prevents despair, and 'the answer now belongs to policy' frames the remaining uncertainty. C — urgently clear-eyed about stakes and open about political response — is the most precise. A is wrong (the question is 'genuinely open'). B is wrong (no optimism expressed). D is wrong (the language is clearly evaluative).

Passage: 'The social media platform's community guidelines document runs to 47 pages. It prohibits 'harmful content' without defining harm. It bans 'coordinated inauthentic behavior' while running an advertising system that allows paid impersonation of grassroots movements. It claims to protect 'user safety' while employing an algorithm that repeatedly shown to recommend increasingly extreme content. The document is a remarkable achievement in the literature of institutional self-description: comprehensive, detailed, sincere-sounding, and substantially disconnected from the actual policies governing the platform.'

The author's attitude toward the platform's community guidelines is best described as
Neutral, describing the contents of the document
Satirically critical — using the document's own contradictions to expose the gap between stated values and actual practice
Alarmed that the platform's algorithm recommends extreme content

'Remarkable achievement in the literature of institutional self-description: comprehensive, detailed, sincere-sounding, and substantially disconnected from actual policies' is a brilliant satirical formulation. The author lists the document's self-contradictions (defines 'harmful' vaguely, bans coordinated inauthentic behavior while enabling paid astroturfing) as evidence of the disconnect. C is correct. A is wrong (it's mock-admiration — irony). B is wrong (the final sentence is explicitly evaluative). D is wrong (the concern is about institutional hypocrisy, not specifically the algorithm).

Passage: 'Twentieth-century philosopher Hannah Arendt's concept of the 'banality of evil' — developed after attending the trial of Nazi administrator Adolf Eichmann — remains one of the most debated and misunderstood concepts in moral and political philosophy. Arendt argued that Eichmann was not a monster but a bureaucrat: someone who committed atrocities not out of ideological fanaticism but out of thoughtlessness — an inability or refusal to think from any perspective other than his bureaucratic role. The concept has been criticized as exculpatory by some scholars and embraced as essential by others. Arendt herself found the controversy distressing, but the concept has proved too generative to be quietly shelved.'

The author's attitude toward Arendt's concept is best described as
Nostalgic for a time when moral philosophy engaged more directly with historical events
Critical of the concept as morally dangerous and exculpatory
Fully endorsing Arendt's argument that Eichmann was not ideologically motivated
Intellectually respectful — treating the concept as significant and generative while accurately representing the debate around it

'One of the most debated and misunderstood concepts' (significant), 'too generative to be quietly shelved' (enduring value) — these show intellectual respect. The author doesn't endorse one side of the scholarly debate (criticized vs. embraced) but presents it accurately. C is correct. A is wrong (the author finds the concept 'too generative to shelve'). B is wrong (the author presents the controversy without fully endorsing Arendt's specific claims). D is wrong (no nostalgia expressed).

Passage: 'The review committee's report identified 23 areas requiring improvement in the organization's data security practices. Management responded by forming a working group to develop a framework for prioritizing which of the 23 areas should be addressed first. Eighteen months later, the working group presented a report recommending the formation of a specialized task force to develop implementation guidelines for the priority areas identified by the working group's framework. The data breach that subsequently affected 4.3 million users occurred before the task force held its first meeting.'

The author's attitude toward the organization's response to the security review is best described as
Sympathetically understanding of the complexities of large-scale security improvements
Mordantly critical — using the sequence of bureaucratic non-action to expose the organization's failure
Alarmed by the specific vulnerabilities identified in the original security review
Neutral, describing the sequence of events that preceded the data breach

The accumulation of procedural inaction — working group → framework → task force → breach before first meeting — without the author ever stating an explicit judgment is SATIRICAL / MORDANTLY CRITICAL. The final sentence ('The data breach... occurred before the task force held its first meeting') is devastating through understatement. C is correct. A is wrong (the selection of these specific details is clearly critical). B is wrong (the events are selected and arranged to make an implicit argument about institutional failure). D is wrong (the specific vulnerabilities are not discussed — the critique is about process).

Text 1: 'Electric vehicles represent the most promising pathway to decarbonizing transportation. Their lifecycle emissions — including manufacturing — are already lower than internal combustion vehicles in most regions and will improve further as the electricity grid becomes cleaner. Mass EV adoption is both technically feasible and economically inevitable.'

Text 2: 'The electric vehicle revolution, while environmentally beneficial in operation, transfers rather than eliminates its environmental costs. Mining lithium, cobalt, and nickel for batteries creates significant ecological damage in producing regions. A more comprehensive transportation policy would prioritize reducing vehicle miles traveled — through urban density, transit, and active transportation — rather than simply swapping one vehicle type for another.'

Based on both texts, the authors would most likely agree that
EVs are the most effective solution to transportation emissions
EVs produce lower operational emissions than gasoline-powered vehicles
Mining for EV batteries is a serious environmental concern requiring policy attention
Reducing total vehicle use is more important than electrifying the existing vehicle fleet

Text 1 says EV lifecycle emissions 'are already lower than internal combustion vehicles.' Text 2 says EVs are 'environmentally beneficial in operation.' Both acknowledge EVs produce lower operational emissions. B is the shared agreement. A is only Text 1's position. C is only Text 2's concern (Text 1 doesn't mention it). D is only Text 2's argument.

Text 1: 'The human memory is fundamentally reconstructive, not reproductive. Each time a memory is retrieved, it is rebuilt from fragments and can be altered by subsequent experience, suggestion, and expectation. This means eyewitness testimony is inherently unreliable as legal evidence.'

Text 2: 'While memory is subject to distortion, the degree of unreliability varies considerably with conditions. Highly distinctive, emotionally salient events are encoded and retained more accurately than ordinary ones. Eyewitness testimony for peripheral details is indeed unreliable, but testimony about the central action in a violent crime may be quite accurate.'

How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
By agreeing that eyewitness testimony should never be used as legal evidence
By arguing that legal reforms have already addressed the problem of unreliable eyewitness testimony
By disputing the claim that human memory is reconstructive rather than reproductive
By arguing that Text 1 overgeneralizes — the reliability of eyewitness testimony varies by emotional significance and detail type

Text 2 acknowledges memory distortion ('while memory is subject to distortion') but argues reliability VARIES — emotionally salient events are more accurate, and central actions more reliable than peripheral details. This directly challenges Text 1's blanket conclusion that eyewitness testimony is 'inherently unreliable.' B is correct. A is wrong (Text 2 argues testimony CAN be reliable). C is wrong (Text 2 doesn't dispute reconstruction — it accepts it but argues it varies). D is wrong (legal reforms not mentioned).

Text 1: 'The decline of local journalism has created communities that are less informed about the decisions of local government and less capable of holding local officials accountable. Studies consistently show that communities without local newspapers have higher municipal borrowing costs, lower voter turnout in local elections, and higher rates of corruption among local officials.'

Text 2: 'The economic model that sustained local journalism — classified advertising revenue — has been permanently disrupted by digital platforms. Subsidizing failing local news outlets would simply delay the inevitable. A better approach invests in new journalistic models: nonprofit newsrooms, local news start-ups, and structured journalism programs at regional universities.'

Which best describes the relationship between the two texts?
Text 2 challenges the claim in Text 1 that local journalism reduces corruption
Text 1 establishes the importance of local journalism; Text 2 accepts this premise and argues for new models to replace the failing old one
The texts present identical solutions to the problem of declining local journalism
The texts disagree about whether local journalism is important for democratic accountability

Text 1 establishes WHY local journalism matters (accountability, corruption, turnout). Text 2 accepts that local journalism is important (doesn't challenge Text 1) but focuses on HOW to sustain it via new models. B correctly identifies this complementary/extension relationship. A is wrong (Text 2 doesn't dispute journalism's importance). C is wrong (Text 2 doesn't challenge Text 1's specific claims). D is wrong (they propose different approaches).

Text 1: 'The concept of 'natural' in food marketing has no scientific basis. 'Natural' flavors can be chemically identical to 'artificial' ones; the difference lies in source, not structure. Regulatory agencies in most countries have declined to define the term, making 'natural' on a food label legally meaningless.'

Text 2: 'Consumer preference for 'natural' products, however scientifically unfounded, is a real and powerful market signal. Companies that ignore it do so at commercial risk. The interesting question is not whether 'natural' is scientifically meaningful but why consumers have developed such strong preferences for naturalness — what psychological and cultural functions the concept serves.'

How would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the focus of Text 2?
By conceding that the scientific meaninglessness of 'natural' is less important than its cultural significance
By suggesting that regulatory agencies should study consumer psychology before defining 'natural'
By arguing that Text 2's acceptance of consumer preferences as a 'market signal' ignores the harm caused by misleading marketing that exploits those preferences
By agreeing that consumer psychology is the most important lens for understanding 'natural' food labeling

Text 1's concern is that 'natural' is misleading and scientifically meaningless. If Text 2 accepts consumer preference as a 'market signal' to be catered to, Text 1's author would argue: this ignores the problem that companies are exploiting a psychologically real but scientifically false belief. B captures this response. A is wrong (Text 1 is critical of the 'natural' concept, not interested in its psychology). C is wrong (Text 1 doesn't concede cultural significance trumps scientific accuracy). D is wrong (not stated).

Text 1: 'Long-form journalism — deeply reported, book-length magazine features — is in crisis. Digital platforms reward brevity and engagement metrics. Advertisers follow eyeballs. The economic incentives that once sustained thousand-word investigations have largely dissolved.'

Text 2: 'The apparent crisis of long-form journalism is a crisis of the legacy advertising model, not of audience appetite. Newsletter platforms, reader-supported journalism, and podcast adaptations of long-form reporting have found substantial audiences willing to pay directly for in-depth work. The business model has changed; the form may survive.'

Based on Text 2, how would its author most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
By suggesting that brief content is preferable to long-form journalism for modern audiences
By arguing that Text 1 conflates the crisis of the advertising model with the fate of long-form journalism as a form, and that direct-support models suggest the form can persist
By arguing that government subsidy is the only path to saving long-form journalism
By agreeing that long-form journalism is disappearing because of digital platforms

Text 2 explicitly says the crisis is 'of the legacy advertising model, not of audience appetite' — directly responding to Text 1's claim that 'economic incentives have dissolved.' Text 2 argues new models (newsletters, direct support) can sustain the form. B accurately captures this reframe. A is wrong (Text 2 argues the form can survive). C is wrong (Text 2 says audience appetite for long-form remains). D is wrong (Text 2 doesn't mention government subsidy).

Text 1: 'Meritocracy — the idea that talent and effort determine success — functions ideologically to legitimate inequality. By attributing success to individual merit, it obscures the structural advantages of birth: inherited wealth, educational access, social networks, and neighborhood resources that compound over generations.'

Text 2: 'Critics of meritocracy often elide an important distinction: between meritocracy as an ideology that naturalizes inequality and meritocracy as an institutional ideal — the aspiration that positions should be allocated based on relevant competence rather than birth, caste, or connection. Rejecting the ideology need not mean rejecting the institutional aspiration.'

Which best describes the relationship between the two texts?
Text 2 refines the argument in Text 1 by distinguishing between meritocracy as ideology (which Text 1 criticizes) and meritocracy as institutional aspiration (which can be defended)
The texts address different topics and cannot be meaningfully compared
Text 2 directly contradicts the central argument of Text 1
The texts are in complete agreement that meritocracy is harmful

Text 2 doesn't fully contradict Text 1 — it accepts the 'ideology' critique while introducing a distinction that partially redeems the concept. This is a REFINING/EXTENSION relationship: Text 2 accepts Text 1's critique of the ideology but argues it doesn't apply to the institutional aspiration. B is correct. A is wrong (Text 2 partially defends meritocracy as aspiration). C is wrong (Text 2 partially accepts Text 1's critique). D is wrong (both address meritocracy directly).

Text 1: 'Mandatory voting — requiring all citizens to vote under penalty of fine — has been implemented successfully in Australia and several other democracies. Turnout exceeds 90%, participation is demographically representative, and the requirement does not appear to compromise the quality of political decisions.'

Text 2: 'Requiring citizens to vote conflates participation with civic virtue. A voter who casts a ballot randomly or out of resentment at being compelled contributes nothing meaningful to democratic deliberation. What democracies need is not higher turnout but more informed, engaged citizenship — qualities that mandates cannot produce and may actively undermine by reducing elections to a compliance exercise.'

Based on Text 1, how would its author most likely respond to the argument in Text 2?
By arguing that Australian evidence shows mandatory voting does not compromise decision quality, directly countering Text 2's concern about uninformed or resentful voters
By conceding that civic virtue cannot be legislated but arguing that turnout matters independently of voter quality
By agreeing that random or resentful voting undermines democratic quality
By suggesting that fines for non-voting are too lenient to motivate genuine civic engagement

Text 1 specifically says mandatory voting 'does not appear to compromise the quality of political decisions' — this directly responds to Text 2's concern that compelled voters contribute nothing meaningful. B applies Text 1's Australian evidence to Text 2's specific concern. A is wrong (Text 1 doesn't agree with this worry — it argues quality is not compromised). C is wrong (Text 1 doesn't make this concession). D is wrong (fine levels are not discussed in Text 1).

Text 1: 'Research on sleep and learning shows that slow-wave sleep is critical for memory consolidation. During slow-wave sleep, newly acquired information is transferred from the hippocampus — a temporary storage area — to the neocortex for long-term retention. Sleep deprivation disrupts this consolidation, causing memories to degrade.'

Text 2: 'REM sleep, long associated with dreaming, also plays a crucial role in memory processing — specifically in the integration of new memories with existing knowledge networks. While slow-wave sleep transfers memories, REM sleep appears to help make those memories meaningful by connecting them to prior experience. The two sleep stages work sequentially to consolidate and contextualize learning.'

Which best describes the relationship between the two texts?
The texts disagree about which sleep stage is more important for memory
Text 2 challenges the claim in Text 1 that slow-wave sleep is critical for memory consolidation
Text 1 provides historical context for the more recent research described in Text 2
Text 2 extends Text 1 by describing a complementary role for REM sleep in memory processing that works alongside the slow-wave sleep process Text 1 describes

Text 2 doesn't challenge Text 1 — it explicitly says 'the two sleep stages work sequentially.' Text 2 ADDS to Text 1 by describing REM sleep's role in contextualization after slow-wave sleep handles transfer. B correctly identifies this extension/complement relationship. A is wrong (no competition between stages — they work together). C is wrong (Text 2 accepts Text 1's claim). D is wrong (no historical framing).

Text 1: 'Gig economy platforms like Uber and Deliveroo have created new forms of precarious employment by classifying workers as independent contractors rather than employees. This classification exempts companies from providing benefits, overtime pay, and job security protections that full-time employees receive, effectively shifting business risk onto individual workers.'

Text 2: 'Gig work offers genuine flexibility that many workers actively prefer over traditional employment. Survey data consistently shows that a significant portion of gig workers chose this arrangement specifically to control their own schedules and supplement other income. Regulating gig work as traditional employment could eliminate the very flexibility that makes it valuable to this segment of workers.'

Based on both texts, both authors would most likely agree that
Gig workers should be classified as employees and receive full benefits
Gig work platforms have changed how some workers earn income
Government regulation of the gig economy is unnecessary
The flexibility of gig work outweighs its risks for most workers

Text 1 says gig platforms have 'created new forms' of employment — acknowledging they exist and changed labor. Text 2 says gig work 'offers genuine flexibility' that workers choose. Both agree gig work platforms have changed how some workers earn income. B is the shared point. A is Text 1's position (Text 2 opposes this). C is Text 2's position (Text 1 opposes this). D is neither author's explicit claim.

Text 1: 'The discovery that epigenetic changes — alterations in gene expression that don't involve changing the DNA sequence — can be inherited across generations challenges the strict Mendelian view that only DNA sequence is heritable. If environmental experiences can alter gene expression in ways that are passed to offspring, our understanding of heredity requires revision.'

Text 2: 'Claims about transgenerational epigenetic inheritance in humans have been overstated. While such inheritance is well-documented in plants and some animals, the evidence in humans is far weaker. Most reported transgenerational effects in human studies have methodological confounds — shared environments, direct biological exposure during pregnancy — that make inheritance of epigenetic changes (as distinct from other mechanisms) difficult to establish.'

How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
By agreeing that Mendelian genetics requires revision in light of epigenetic research
By disputing that epigenetic changes involve alterations in gene expression
By suggesting that Text 1 is correct about plants and animals but not about humans
By arguing that the evidence for transgenerational epigenetic inheritance specifically in humans does not yet warrant revising our understanding of human heredity

Text 2 argues that while epigenetic inheritance exists in plants and animals, human evidence is weak and methodologically confounded. This means Text 2 would challenge Text 1's conclusion that 'our understanding of heredity requires revision' — at least regarding humans. B captures this: the human evidence doesn't yet justify the revision Text 1 calls for. A is wrong (Text 2 resists this revision for humans). C is technically right but B is more precise about WHY (the human evidence is weak). D is wrong (Text 2 doesn't dispute the definition of epigenetic changes).

Text 1: 'Modern cities have systematically underinvested in public spaces — parks, plazas, libraries, and community centers — in favor of private commercial development. This has eroded the 'third places' where citizens of different backgrounds might encounter one another outside of home and work, contributing to social fragmentation and distrust.'

Text 2: 'The internet and social media have created new forms of third place — online communities where people build relationships, share interests, and form identities. While these digital spaces lack the serendipitous cross-class encounter that urban theorists prize, they have enabled connections across geographic barriers that physical third places rarely achieved. The concept of third place needs updating for a digital age.'

Which best describes the relationship between the two texts?
Text 2 contradicts Text 1 by arguing that social fragmentation has not actually increased
Text 1 and Text 2 address entirely different aspects of urban planning and cannot be compared
Text 2 challenges Text 1's implicit assumption that meaningful community requires physical space by arguing that digital spaces now serve a similar social function
The texts agree that physical public spaces are more important than digital ones

Text 1 implicitly assumes community requires PHYSICAL third places. Text 2 challenges this by arguing digital spaces now serve similar social functions. B correctly identifies this challenge to Text 1's assumption. A is wrong (they disagree about relative importance). C is wrong (both address where community forms). D is wrong (Text 2 doesn't address social fragmentation trends).

Text 1: 'The Anthropocene — the proposed geological epoch defined by human impact on Earth systems — should be formally recognized. The stratigraphic record already shows clear human signatures: plastics, nuclear fallout, and novel mineral compounds deposited globally since the mid-twentieth century. This boundary is as real as any other in the geological record.'

Text 2: 'The proposed Anthropocene epoch faces a fundamental problem: the geological record already preserves a rich record of earlier human impacts, from deforestation pollen signatures dating to early agriculture to megafauna extinctions associated with human arrival. Selecting the mid-twentieth century as the boundary is a choice reflecting contemporary concerns, not a uniquely clear stratigraphic signal.'

Based on Text 1, how would its author most likely respond to the argument in Text 2?
By conceding that the Anthropocene boundary is culturally rather than scientifically determined
By agreeing that earlier human impacts complicate the Anthropocene boundary
By suggesting that the geological record before the twentieth century shows no evidence of human impact

By arguing that the mid-twentieth century deposits — plastics, nuclear fallout, novel compounds — represent a qualitatively different and globally synchronous signal absent from earlier human impacts, justifying the specific boundary proposed

Text 1 specifically cites mid-twentieth century deposits (plastics, nuclear fallout, novel mineral compounds) as the basis for the boundary — implying these are qualitatively distinctive. In response to Text 2's argument that earlier impacts also exist, Text 1's author would emphasize what makes the mid-twentieth century signal DIFFERENT: global synchrony and novel compound types. B captures this defense. A is wrong (Text 1 would argue the distinction is real, not merely a contemporary concern). C is wrong (Text 1 argues the boundary is scientifically real). D is wrong (Text 1 doesn't deny earlier human impacts).

Text 1: 'The opioid epidemic has been framed primarily as a law enforcement problem — drug trafficking, dealer prosecution, and user criminalization. This framing has proven counterproductive. Treating addiction as a criminal rather than a medical matter drives users away from treatment, creates legal records that limit employment and housing, and does nothing to address the pharmaceutical and medical practices that created the epidemic.'

Text 2: 'Decriminalizing drug use without simultaneously expanding treatment infrastructure and addressing social determinants of addiction — poverty, trauma, isolation — simply replaces one failed approach with another. Oregon's decriminalization experiment, which created pathways to treatment without funding them adequately, has produced mixed results at best. Policy reform requires investment as much as legal change.'

Based on both texts, both authors would most likely agree that
Pharmaceutical companies bear primary responsibility for the opioid epidemic
Addressing addiction requires approaches that extend beyond criminal prosecution and include treatment and social factors
Drug use should be fully legalized rather than merely decriminalized
Current law enforcement approaches to addiction have been adequate

Text 1 argues criminalization is counterproductive and doesn't address medical/pharmaceutical causes. Text 2 argues decriminalization alone is insufficient without treatment and addressing social determinants. Both agree that criminal prosecution alone is inadequate and that treatment/social factors are necessary. C captures this shared ground. A is neither text's claim. B is directly contradicted by Text 1. D is only mentioned in Text 1 and even there not as the 'primary' responsibility claim.

'Severely compromised' = seriously damaged — appropriate for a critical policy review. C is correct. A and D are neutral. B is too vague.

Paragraph focus: long-term health effects of air pollution. Proposed deletion: 'Air pollution is a major environmental problem globally.'

Should this be kept or deleted?
Deleted — it is too general to advance the specific discussion of long-term health effects; the paragraph needs specific evidence, not vague statements
'Air pollution is a major environmental problem' is too vague to serve as evidence for long-term health effects. C is correct.

Text: 'The results [___] that mindfulness training may reduce anxiety symptoms, at least in the short term.'

Context: A small pilot study (n=30).

Which word best fits?
Small pilot study (n=30) → hedging language. D (suggest) is appropriately cautious. A, B, C overclaim for a pilot study.

Sentence for placement: 'The following examples illustrate how this pattern manifests in practice.'

Paragraph: '[1] Research shows a consistent link between income inequality and poor health outcomes. [2] Low-income individuals have higher rates of chronic disease. [3] Life expectancy differs dramatically across income levels.'

Where does it fit best?
After S1 (establishes the pattern) → 'following examples illustrate the pattern in practice' signals that S2 and S3 are examples. After 1 is correct.

Text: 'The novel's [___] prose style forces readers to slow down and confront the weight of each sentence.'

Which word best fits?

'Deliberate' = intentionally measured — positive connotation matching 'forces readers to confront each sentence.' B is correct. A and C have negative connotations. D (labored) suggests difficult/strained effort.

Paragraph focus: improvements in global child mortality. Proposed addition: 'UNICEF was founded in 1946.'

Should this be added?
Yes — UNICEF is relevant to child health
No — UNICEF's founding date doesn't directly support or advance the discussion of mortality improvements
UNICEF's founding date is a historical fact tangential to mortality improvement trends. C is correct.

Passage: Although the committee's report was widely praised for its rigor, several economists found its conclusions ______, noting that the data could just as easily support the opposite interpretation.

Which choice best completes the text?

The clue is that the data could support the opposite interpretation, so the conclusions are open to more than one reading — 'equivocal.' 'Unambiguous' is the opposite; 'meticulous' and 'exhaustive' praise the rigor, not the uncertainty.

Passage: Far from being a ______ figure, the novelist courted controversy at every turn, delighting in the outrage her public statements provoked.

Which choice best completes the text?

'Far from being' signals a contrast with courting controversy, so the blank needs a word meaning shy or withdrawn — 'retiring.' 'Provocative,' 'polarizing,' and 'notorious' all match (not contrast) her controversial behavior.
Expression of Ideas:

European coffeehouses, which first opened in the 17th century, played an important role in the development of intellectual and commercial culture.
Coffee has a rich history spanning more than a thousand years, from its origins in Ethiopia to its current global presence.
Medium
Rhetorical Synthesis
Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to establish GLOBAL SIGNIFICANCE. B uses the two most impactful statistics: 2 billion cups daily AND second most traded commodity — both directly establish significance. A only covers the historical spread (not significance). C focuses on coffeehouses (historical context, not global significance). D is vague and doesn't use specific data to establish significance.

The record global temperatures of 2023 and the concurrent record low Arctic sea ice extent represent evidence of accelerating change in Earth's climate systems.

Polar ice sheets hold approximately 68% of Earth's fresh water, meaning their complete melting would raise sea levels by approximately 70 meters.
Sea levels are currently rising at approximately 3.6 millimeters per year, and polar ice sheets contain approximately 68% of Earth's fresh water.

Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to support 'accelerating change' using RECENT DATA. B uses 2023 record temperatures and record low Arctic sea ice — both from 2023 and explicitly described as 'accelerating change.' Founded in 1800, the Library of Congress holds approximately 173 million items and has evolved from a congressional resource to a public institution.

While the Library of Congress holds the historic 1507 map that first named 'America,' its collections extend far beyond historical documents to include Stradivari violins — instruments still used in active performances hosted by the institution.
The Library of Congress holds 173 million items and is open to the public without requiring a library card for on-site research.
The Library of Congress, founded in 1800 to serve the US Congress, has grown into a public research institution holding approximately 173 million items.

Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to emphasize 'unexpected breadth — far more than books and documents.' Counterintuitively, some urban environments now support healthier bee populations than adjacent rural agricultural areas — a finding that complicates the narrative of universal decline.
Urban beekeeping has increased by 200% in the past five years, reflecting growing public awareness of the importance of pollinators.
Bees pollinate approximately one-third of the world's food supply, making their documented 30% population decline over the past decade a serious concern for global agriculture.

Rhetorical Synthesis

The Mona Lisa, painted by Leonardo da Vinci over approximately sixteen years from 1503 to 1519, is protected by bullet-resistant glass following a 1956 acid attack.

A painting smaller than a kitchen cabinet door — measuring 77 × 53 centimeters — draws approximately 10 million visitors annually to the Louvre, making the Mona Lisa one of the starkest examples of the gap between an artwork's physical scale and its cultural significance.

Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to create a CONTRAST between physical smallness and cultural magnitude. Notes:

• Social/behavioral factors: men more likely to smoke, drink excessively, avoid healthcare

Women outlive men by approximately 5 years globally, a gap that in the US reached 5.7 years in 2020.

Medium
Rhetorical Synthesis
Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to support the claim about BOTH biological and social factors. B explicitly names both categories with specific examples from each: biological (estrogen, immune differences) and social/behavioral (smoking, drinking, healthcare avoidance). Rome's free grain distribution program, known as the 'dole,' served up to 200,000 male citizens and helped stabilize the city's social order.

The 11 aqueducts that supplied ancient Rome with water represent a remarkable feat of engineering that has influenced water infrastructure design for centuries.

Rhetorical Synthesis
Rhetorical Synthesis

In wealthy nations, food waste occurs primarily at the consumer and retail stages, while in developing countries, loss occurs earlier in the supply chain during harvest and storage.
Reducing food waste has been identified as one of the most high-impact interventions available for addressing climate change, according to multiple environmental analyses.
Approximately 40% of global food is wasted, and if this waste were attributed to a single country, it would rank as the third largest greenhouse gas emitter globally.

Food waste — which generates greenhouse gas emissions comparable to the world's third largest country if considered a single emitter — occurs through different mechanisms in wealthy and developing nations, suggesting that effective solutions must be tailored to economic context.

Rhetorical Synthesis

Michelangelo created three of the Renaissance's most celebrated works — the Pietà, David, and the Sistine Chapel — across a remarkably productive career.
Michelangelo famously described his creative process as liberating the form already present within the marble, suggesting an intuitive rather than technical approach to sculpture.

Rhetorical Synthesis

Rhetorical Synthesis

Notes:
• Antarctic ice sheet contains 60% of Earth's fresh water
• Antarctica receives less annual precipitation than the Sahara Desert

Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is an UNEXPECTED PARALLEL that makes Antarctica PARADOXICALLY RELEVANT to understanding Earth's water. Notes:

Rhetorical Synthesis

The Amazon River system, which contains more fish species than any other river in the world and is home to one of only five freshwater dolphin species globally, represents an ecosystem of unparalleled biodiversity among the world's river systems.
The Amazon River drains approximately 40% of South America and discharges approximately 20% of all fresh water entering the world's oceans.
Medium
Rhetorical Synthesis
Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to establish ECOLOGICAL UNIQUENESS among river systems. B uses two uniqueness markers: most fish species of any river AND one of only five freshwater dolphin species globally — both comparative and explicitly establishing uniqueness 'among the world's river systems.' Notes:

• 2020 study: sepsis algorithm less likely to flag Black patients for intervention

AI diagnostic tools trained on non-diverse datasets raise important questions about equity in healthcare delivery and the responsibility of technology developers.
Medium
Rhetorical Synthesis
Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to ESTABLISH A PATTERN through multiple examples. B uses three specific examples from the notes (blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, sepsis algorithms) in a list that explicitly identifies 'a pattern of non-representative testing' — perfectly achieving the pattern-establishing goal. A presents the FDA response but only one data point. C provides one example only. D is vague and doesn't cite specific examples.

Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal requires BOTH acknowledging historical recognition AND emphasizing institutional barriers. Notes:

Rhetorical Synthesis
Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to argue QUALITY over QUANTITY of protection. B uses the 'paper parks' statistic (50% of parks inadequately managed) to argue that quality of protection matters more than the quantity/acreage — directly supporting the quality-over-quantity argument. A focuses on the quantity gap (12% vs 30%) — supporting expanding quantity, not the quality argument. C uses indigenous management but as a comparison, not directly making the quality-over-quantity argument. D focuses on expansion needs — the quantity approach.

• His notebooks were lost for approximately 200 years after his death
• Some designs have since been shown to be physically workable when built

The goal requires BOTH 'uniquely American cultural synthesis' AND 'global impact.' B covers both: the synthesis (African + European traditions combining in American context), the global spread (1920s recordings), and the global impact (shaped rock, hip-hop, 'virtually all subsequent popular music worldwide'). A establishes the synthesis origin but not the global impact. C describes the global spread but not the synthesis aspect explicitly. Amelia Earhart accumulated extraordinary achievements — including the first solo transatlantic flight by a woman and multiple speed and altitude records — before her disappearance over the Pacific in 1937, which remains unexplained despite decades of investigation and recent underwater searches, ensuring her legacy is inseparable from mystery.

Rhetorical Synthesis

Dogs can distinguish only blue and yellow tones, while humans can perceive approximately 10 million colors — a comparison that illustrates the extraordinary variability of visual systems across species.

While humans perceive 10 million colors through three receptor types, the mantis shrimp processes visual information through 16 receptor types, many birds and insects perceive ultraviolet light invisible to humans, and deep-sea fish detect bioluminescence beyond human visual range — a comparative survey that reveals human color vision as one specialized system among many rather than a universal standard.

Rhetorical Synthesis

The goal is to use CONTRAST to challenge the assumption that HUMAN COLOR VISION is the norm. B presents multiple contrasts: mantis shrimp (16 receptors > 3), birds/insects (see UV invisible to humans), deep-sea fish (detect bioluminescence humans can't) — and explicitly concludes that human vision is 'one specialized system among many rather than a universal standard.' Henrietta Lacks' cancer cells, taken without her consent in 1951, became the first immortal human cell line and have since been used in research leading to the polio vaccine, cancer treatments, and COVID-19 vaccines.
HeLa cells, derived from Henrietta Lacks' cancer tissue without her knowledge, have been used in the development of some of the most significant medical advances of the past 70 years.

The HeLa cell line's extraordinary scientific utility has generated enormous commercial value for the biotechnology industry, raising important questions about the fair distribution of benefits from medical research.

CBT is an evidence-based treatment for depression, anxiety, and PTSD, and digital platforms now make variations of this treatment accessible without the need for a therapist.

The goal requires BOTH supporting iCBT for EXPANDING ACCESS AND acknowledging a KEY LIMITATION. Text: 'The council decided to postpone and delay the vote until a later date in the future.'

Which choice most effectively revises the sentence to eliminate unnecessary repetition?
The council decided to postpone the vote.
The council decided to later postpone and delay the vote.
The council decided to postpone and delay the vote to a future date.
The council decided to postpone and delay the vote until a later date in the future.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Postpone' and 'delay' are synonyms (redundant pair). 'Until a later date in the future' — 'later date' and 'in the future' both mean the same thing, and 'postpone' already implies moving to a future time. B keeps only the essential meaning.

Text: 'The reason the project failed was because the team lacked adequate resources.'

Which choice most effectively revises the underlined portion?
The reason the project failed was that the team lacked adequate resources.
The reason for which the project failed was because the team lacked in adequate resources.
The reason the project failed was because the team lacked adequate resources.
The project failed due to the fact that there was a lack of adequate resources on the team.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'The reason was because' is redundant — 'because' already introduces a reason. The correct form is 'the reason was that.' B makes this correction. A keeps the error. C adds 'due to the fact that' (wordy). D is grammatically awkward and keeps 'because.'

Text: 'The completely exhausted marathon runners finally crossed the finish line at the end of the race.'

Which revision most effectively eliminates redundancy?
The marathon runners, who were exhausted, finally crossed the finish line at the end of the race.
The completely exhausted marathon runners finally crossed the finish line at the end of the race.
The completely exhausted and very tired marathon runners finally crossed the finish line at the end of the race.
The exhausted marathon runners crossed the finish line.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Completely exhausted' — 'completely' is a meaningless intensifier (you're either exhausted or you're not). 'At the end of the race' is implied by 'crossing the finish line.' B removes both. A keeps both. C adds 'and very tired' (redundant with exhausted). D keeps 'at the end of the race.'

Text: 'Due to the fact that the medication has the ability to cause serious side effects, patients should consult their doctors.'

Which revision is most concise without losing meaning?
Because the medication can cause serious side effects, patients should consult their doctors.
Due to the fact that the medication has the ability to cause serious side effects, patients should consult their doctors.
As a result of the fact that the medication possesses the ability to cause serious side effects, patients should consult with their doctors.
The medication has the ability to cause serious side effects, which is the reason why patients should consult their doctors.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Due to the fact that' → 'because' | 'has the ability to' → 'can.' B applies both concisions. A keeps both wordy phrases. C replaces one wordy phrase with an even wordier one. D keeps 'has the ability to' and adds 'which is the reason why.'

Text: 'Scientists made an unexpected and surprising discovery about the origins of the universe.'

Which revision eliminates the redundancy?
Scientists made a surprising discovery about the origins of the universe.
Scientists made an unexpected and surprising discovery about the origins of the universe.
Scientists made a very unexpected discovery that was surprising about the origins of the universe.
Scientists made a discovery that was both unexpected and also surprising about the origins of the universe.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Unexpected' and 'surprising' are synonyms when describing a discovery — a redundant pair. B keeps just 'surprising.' A keeps both. C adds 'very' and rephrases awkwardly. D adds 'both...and also' (more words, same redundancy).

Text: 'The new policy will help facilitate the improvement of working conditions for employees at the company.'

Which is the most concise revision?
The new policy has the ability to help in the facilitation of improvements to employee working conditions.
The new policy will facilitate the improvement and betterment of working conditions for all employees at the company.
The new policy will help improve working conditions for employees.
The new policy will help facilitate the improvement of working conditions for employees at the company.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Help facilitate the improvement of' → 'help improve' (three words become two). 'At the company' is contextually implied when talking about a company policy. B is maximally concise. A is wordy. C adds 'betterment' (redundant with improvement). D is much wordier.

Text: 'The ancient ruins, which were old and dated back thousands of years, attracted tourists from around the world.'

Which revision is most effective?
The ancient ruins, which were old and dated back thousands of years, attracted tourists from around the world.
The ancient ruins, which dated back thousands of years, attracted tourists from around the world.
The old, ancient ruins, which were thousands of years old, attracted tourists from around the world.
The ruins, which were ancient and dated back many thousands of years into the past, attracted tourists from around the world.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Ancient ruins which were old' — 'ancient' and 'old' are redundant. 'Dated back thousands of years' shows age, making 'which were old' doubly redundant. B removes 'which were old' and 'ancient' (keeping 'ancient' in the main noun is actually better than the clause). A keeps all redundancies. C has 'old, ancient' (redundant pair). D has 'many thousands of years into the past' ('into the past' is redundant with 'dated back').

Text: 'In the event that the experiment produces unexpected results, researchers should document and record all observations.'

Which revision is most concise?

If the experiment produces unexpected results, researchers should document all observations.
In the event that the experiment produces unexpected results, researchers should document and record all observations.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'In the event that' → 'if' (4 words → 1). 'Document and record' — redundant pair; 'document' includes recording. B applies both concisions. A keeps both. C adds 'in nature' and 'ought to document and record.' D keeps 'in the event that' and adds 'make documentation and recordings.'

Text: 'The athlete was able to successfully complete the marathon in under three hours.'

Which revision eliminates the redundancy?
The athlete was able to and did successfully complete the marathon in under three hours.
The athlete was able to successfully complete the marathon in under three hours.
The athlete completed the marathon in under three hours.
The athlete was successful in being able to complete the marathon in a time under three hours.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Was able to' and 'successfully' are both implied by 'complete' — if you complete something, you were able to do it and you did it successfully. B strips both. A keeps both. C adds 'in a time under' (wordy). D adds 'and did.'

Text: 'The report's findings were both important and significant to the future advancement of the field.'

The report's findings were significant for the advancement of the field.
The report's findings were important, significant, and consequential for the future of the field.
The report's findings were both important and significant to the future advancement of the field.
The report's findings were very important and quite significant for the future advancement of the field.

Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Important and significant' — redundant pair. 'Future advancement' — 'advancement' implies moving forward (future is redundant). B removes the redundant pair and 'future.' A keeps both. C adds a third synonym ('consequential'). D adds intensifiers ('very,' 'quite').

Text: 'The new bridge design incorporates several different features that are unique and one-of-a-kind.'

The new bridge design, which is new, incorporates several different and varied unique features.

The new bridge design incorporates several different features that are unique and one-of-a-kind.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Different' is redundant with 'several' (several already implies differences). 'Unique' and 'one-of-a-kind' are synonyms. 'That are' is a wordy relative clause replaceable by an adjective. B strips all: 'several unique features.' A keeps all redundancies. C triples the synonyms. D adds 'which is new' (already in 'new bridge design') and 'different and varied.'

Text: 'The new software was designed with the purpose of helping users organize their files more efficiently.'

Text: 'The researchers concluded that the new drug treatment was more effective as compared to the existing standard treatment.'

Text: 'The artist's early paintings, created during the beginning of her career, show remarkable technical skill.'

Text: 'The experiment yielded results that were positive and encouraging for the team.'

yielded encouraging results

Sentence Revision & Clarity

Text: 'The bridge was first constructed in 1923 and has been standing for over 100 years since then.'

was constructed and built in 1923 and has been standing and existing for over 100 years
was first constructed in 1923 and has been first standing for over 100 years
was constructed in 1923 and has stood for over a century
was first constructed in 1923 and has been standing for over 100 years since then

Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Over 100 years' → 'over a century' is a natural and slightly more elegant equivalent. B removes 'first' and 'since then' and uses 'century.' A keeps 'first' and 'since then.' C adds 'first standing.' D has two redundant pairs ('constructed and built,' 'standing and existing').

Text: 'The documentary film provided new and fresh insights into the daily life of deep-sea creatures.'

Which revision is most effective?
provided insights that were both new and fresh into the daily life of deep-sea creatures
provided fresh insights into the daily lives of deep-sea creatures
provided new and fresh insights into the daily life of deep-sea creatures
provided new, fresh, and original insights into the daily life of deep-sea creatures

Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'New and fresh' are synonymous in this context — redundant pair. B keeps only 'fresh.' 'Daily lives' (plural) is also more accurate when referring to multiple creatures. A keeps the redundant pair. C adds 'original' (third synonym). D restructures but keeps both.

Text: 'The CEO personally met with each and every member of the board individually.'

Which revision most effectively eliminates redundancy?
personally met with each and every member of the board individually
met with each individual member of the board in person
met with each board member
personally met with each and every individual member of the board

Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Personally met' and 'individually' both mean meeting one-on-one — redundant. 'Each and every' is a redundant pair. B: 'met with each board member' — three redundancies removed. A keeps all. C adds 'individual' to 'each and every.' D keeps 'individual' and adds 'in person.'

Text: 'The historian argued that these past historical events have been consistently misrepresented over time.'

Which revision eliminates the redundancy?
these past historical events have been time and again repeatedly misrepresented over time
these historical events have been consistently misrepresented
these past historical events have been consistently misrepresented over time
these past historical events have been misrepresented consistently and repeatedly over time
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Past historical' — 'historical' already refers to the past; 'past' is redundant. 'Over time' is implied by 'consistently misrepresented' (which suggests it happened repeatedly over a period). B removes both. A keeps both. C has 'time and again repeatedly' (redundant pair). D has 'consistently and repeatedly' (redundant pair).

Text: 'The policy change will result in a reduction and decrease of administrative costs for the organization.'

Which is most concise?
will result in a reduction, decrease, and lowering of administrative costs
will reduce administrative costs
will result in a reduction and decrease of administrative costs for the organization
will result in administrative cost reductions and decreases for the organization
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Result in a reduction and decrease of' → 'reduce' (six words → one). 'Reduction and decrease' is also a redundant pair. B: 'will reduce administrative costs.' A keeps both issues. C adds 'lowering' (third synonym). D keeps 'reductions and decreases.'

Text: 'The museum's new exhibition features rare and uncommon artifacts from ancient civilizations.'

Which revision is most effective?
features rare and uncommon artifacts from ancient civilizations
features rare artifacts from ancient civilizations
features artifacts that are rare and uncommon from ancient civilizations
features rare, uncommon, and infrequently seen artifacts from ancient civilizations

Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

Text: 'Researchers are currently in the process of developing a more efficient battery technology.'

Which is most concise?
are currently in the process of developing a more efficient battery technology at this point in time
are developing more efficient battery technology
are currently in the process of developing a more efficient battery technology
are currently in the process of and actively developing a more efficient battery technology
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Currently in the process of developing' → 'developing' ('currently' and 'in the process of' both add no information to a present progressive verb). B: 'are developing more efficient battery technology.' A is the wordy original. C adds 'at this point in time.' D adds 'and actively.'

Text: 'The author's prose style is characterized by the use of long, complex sentences that are lengthy and elaborate.'

Which revision is most effective?
is characterized by the use of long, complex, and elaborate sentences that are wordy and lengthy
is characterized by long, lengthy sentences of a complex and elaborate nature
is characterized by the use of long, complex sentences that are lengthy and elaborate
is characterized by long, complex sentences

Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'The use of' → remove (implied by 'characterized by'). 'Long' and 'lengthy' are synonyms. 'Complex' and 'elaborate' overlap significantly. B: 'characterized by long, complex sentences' — removes 'the use of,' 'lengthy' (redundant with long), and 'elaborate' (redundant with complex). A keeps all. C adds 'wordy and lengthy.' D has multiple redundant pairs.

Text: 'Many people believe that Shakespeare wrote his plays alone by himself without any assistance.'

Which revision most effectively eliminates redundancy?
wrote his plays by himself and without any assistance from other people
wrote his plays entirely by himself without any collaborative assistance from others
wrote his plays alone
wrote his plays alone by himself without any assistance
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Alone,' 'by himself,' and 'without any assistance' all convey the same meaning — triple redundancy. B keeps only 'alone.' A keeps all three. C adds 'entirely' and 'collaborative...from others.' D keeps two of the three.

Text: 'The preliminary initial findings of the study suggest that screen time affects sleep quality in adolescents.'

Which revision eliminates the redundancy?
The preliminary findings of the study suggest
The findings of the study, which were both preliminary and initial, suggest
The very preliminary and initial early findings of the study suggest
The preliminary initial findings of the study suggest
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity
'Preliminary' and 'initial' are synonyms — redundant pair. B keeps only 'preliminary.' A keeps both. C triples with 'early.' D restructures but keeps both.

Text: 'The journalist wrote an article exposing corruption in the government, which led to significant public outcry and protest.'

Which revision most effectively addresses redundancy?
which led to public outcry and protest that was significant and widespread
which led to significant public outcry and protest
which led to significant public protest and outcry and demonstrations
which led to significant public outcry
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Outcry' and 'protest' overlap heavily when both modify 'public' — they describe the same collective reaction. B keeps only 'outcry' (which encompasses the protest element). A keeps both. C adds 'demonstrations' (third item). D adds 'widespread' and restructures redundantly.

Text: 'The scientists had previously assumed that the planet was uninhabitable prior to the discovery.'

Which revision is most concise?
had previously assumed that the planet was uninhabitable prior to the discovery
assumed that the planet was uninhabitable prior to the discovery beforehand
had previously and beforehand assumed the planet was uninhabitable prior to the discovery
had assumed the planet was uninhabitable before the discovery
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Previously' and 'prior to the discovery' both convey 'before the discovery' — the time reference is doubled. B: 'had assumed the planet was uninhabitable before the discovery' — keeps one time reference. A keeps two time references. C adds 'and beforehand' (third). D has 'prior to' and 'beforehand' (two redundancies).

Passage: 'Bees pollinate about one-third of the food that humans consume. They are beneficial insects that are very important to agriculture.'

Which revision most effectively combines the two sentences?
Bees pollinate about one-third of the food that humans consume, and they are beneficial insects that are very important to agriculture.
Crucial to agriculture, bees pollinate approximately one-third of the food humans consume.
Bees are beneficial and important insects, and they pollinate about one-third of the food that humans consume.
Bees pollinate about one-third of the food that humans consume, and this makes them beneficial and important.
Medium
Revision
Sentence Revision & Clarity

Sentence 2's content ('beneficial insects, very important to agriculture') largely repeats what sentence 1 already implies. B combines both into one sentence that preserves all necessary information concisely: the agricultural importance ('crucial to agriculture') and the specific contribution (pollinating one-third of food). A combines with no concision. C loses 'agriculture' and adds 'makes them.' D leads with vague 'beneficial and important' then adds the specific fact.

Text: 'The conference was attended by experts from various different fields of study.'

Which revision is most effective?
by experts from various different fields of study
by experts from various and different fields of academic study
by various different experts from a range of different fields
by experts from various fields
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Various' and 'different' are synonyms — redundant pair. 'Of study' is implied by 'fields' in an academic conference context. B: 'by experts from various fields.' A keeps 'various different' and 'of study.' C has multiple 'different' uses. D keeps the redundant pair and adds 'academic.'

Passage: 'The city built new parks to give residents a place to relax. These parks also provided areas for community events.'

Which revision most effectively combines these sentences?
The city built new parks for residents to relax in and host community events.
The city built new parks, which were built to relax in and host community events.
The city built new parks, giving residents places to both relax and host community events.
The city built new parks to give residents a place to relax, and these parks also provided areas for community events.
Medium
Revision
Sentence Revision & Clarity

D combines both purposes ('relax' and 'host community events') cleanly with 'giving residents places to both...and...' — parallel structure, no repetition of 'parks.' B is almost as good but 'for residents to relax in and host' is slightly ambiguous (who hosts?). A repeats 'parks' and 'also provided areas.' C has 'parks, which were built' — awkward and redundant.

Text: 'The company's financial report showed that profits had grown by 15 percent compared to the profits from the previous year.'

Which is the most effective revision?
that profits had grown by 15 percent compared to the profits from the previous year
that profits had grown, specifically by an amount equal to 15 percent, compared to last year's profits
that profits had grown 15 percent year over year
that profits from this year had grown by 15 percent when they are compared to last year's profits
Medium
Precision
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Compared to the profits from the previous year' → 'year over year' is a concise industry-standard expression that eliminates the need to restate 'profits' and 'previous year.' B: 'grown 15 percent year over year.' A is the wordy original (repeats 'profits'). C adds 'specifically by an amount equal to.' D is significantly wordier.

Text: 'The construction of the new highway will help facilitate easier and more convenient access to the downtown area.'

Which revision is most effective?
will improve access to downtown
will help facilitate better, easier, and more convenient access to the downtown area
will help facilitate easier and more convenient access to the downtown area
will help in facilitating more easy and convenient access to downtown areas
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Help facilitate' → 'improve' (shorter and more direct). 'Easier and more convenient' are redundant as applied to access. 'The downtown area' → 'downtown.' B: 'will improve access to downtown.' A is the wordy original. C is worse. D adds 'better' (third synonym).

Text: 'Scientists studying the migration patterns of birds have found that birds migrate further than previously expected.'

Which revision most effectively eliminates redundancy?
Scientists studying bird migration have found that birds travel farther than previously expected.
Scientists who study the migration patterns of birds have found that the birds that they study migrate further than previously expected.
Scientists studying the migration patterns of birds have found that birds migrate further and farther than was previously expected.
Scientists studying the migration patterns of birds have found that birds migrate further than previously expected.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Migration patterns of birds' → 'bird migration' (shorter). 'Further' and 'farther' are used together in D (redundant). B makes the concision without losing meaning. A keeps the longer phrase. C is much wordier. D has 'further and farther' (redundant pair) and 'was previously expected' (wordier).

Text: 'The new curriculum was designed with the goal of teaching critical thinking skills to students.'

Which is most concise?
was designed to teach students critical thinking skills
was designed with the goal of teaching critical thinking skills to students
was designed for the purpose and goal of teaching critical thinking skills to students
was designed in order to teach critical thinking skills to students in the classroom
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'With the goal of teaching' → 'to teach' (4 words → 2). 'To students' can be placed more naturally. B: 'was designed to teach students critical thinking skills.' A is the wordy original. C adds 'for the purpose and goal of.' D adds 'in order to' and 'in the classroom.'

Passage: 'The old bridge was too narrow for modern traffic. Engineers decided to build a new one in the same location.'

Which revision most effectively combines these sentences?
Because the old bridge was too narrow for modern traffic, engineers designed a replacement at the same site.
Engineers decided to build a new bridge because the old bridge was too narrow for modern traffic.
The old bridge was too narrow for modern traffic, and engineers decided to build a new one in the same location.
The old bridge was narrow, so engineers built a new bridge in the same location where the old bridge had been.
Medium
Revision
Sentence Revision & Clarity

B combines the sentences with a causal connection ('because') that's implied but cleaner than 'and,' and uses 'replacement' (more precise than 'new one') and 'site' (more concise than 'same location'). A uses a weak 'and' connection. C repeats 'bridge' twice and adds 'where the old bridge had been' (implied by 'same location'). D is fine but less concise than B.

Text: 'The documentary examines the profound and deep impact that industrialization had on the natural environment.'

Which revision is most effective?
examines the profound and deep impact that industrialization had on the natural environment
examines the very profound and deeply deep impact that industrialization had on the natural environment
examines industrialization's profound impact on the natural environment
examines the profound and deeply significant impact that industrialization had on the natural environment
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Profound' and 'deep' are redundant when modifying impact. 'Industrialization's profound impact on the natural environment' uses a possessive to eliminate 'that industrialization had on.' B is most concise and precise. A keeps the redundant pair. C intensifies both (worse). D replaces 'deep' with 'deeply significant' (still redundant).

Passage: 'The artist spent years developing her unique style. This style blended traditional techniques with modern concepts.'

Which most effectively combines the sentences?
The artist spent years developing her style, a unique style that blended traditional techniques with modern concepts.
The artist, who spent years developing her unique style, blended traditional techniques with modern concepts.
The artist spent years developing her unique style, and this style blended traditional techniques with modern concepts.
The artist spent years developing her unique style, which blended traditional techniques with modern concepts.
Medium
Revision
Sentence Revision & Clarity

B uses a relative clause to combine naturally: 'developing her unique style, which blended traditional techniques with modern concepts' — no repetition of 'style.' A repeats 'style' unnecessarily. C repeats 'style' and adds 'a unique style that.' D changes meaning (artist blended, not style).

Text: 'The report, which was written by the committee, was submitted to the board.'

Which revision most effectively improves clarity and concision?
The report, which was written by the committee, was submitted to the board.
The committee wrote the report and then submitted it to the board.
The report that was written by the committee was subsequently submitted to the board.
The committee's report was submitted to the board.
Medium
Revision
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'The report, which was written by the committee' → 'The committee's report' (possessive eliminates the relative clause). B is the most concise. A uses a wordy relative clause. C adds 'subsequently.' D splits into two clauses unnecessarily.

Text: 'The results of the study were analyzed in order to determine whether there was a connection between the two variables.'

Which is most concise?
