were analyzed to determine whether the variables were connected
were analyzed for the purpose of determining whether there was a possible connection between the two variables
were analyzed in order to determine if there was a connection and relationship between the two variables
were analyzed in order to determine whether there was a connection between the two variables
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'In order to determine' → 'to determine.' 'Whether there was a connection between the two variables' → 'whether the variables were connected.' B: 'were analyzed to determine whether the variables were connected.' A is wordy. C adds 'and relationship' (redundant with connection). D adds 'for the purpose of' and 'possible.'

Text: 'The volcano's recent eruption, which happened recently, caused widespread destruction in the surrounding region.'

Which revision eliminates the redundancy?
The volcano's recent eruption, which happened recently, caused widespread destruction in the surrounding region.
The volcano's recent eruption, occurring recently in a sudden manner, caused widespread destruction.
The volcano's recent eruption caused widespread destruction in the surrounding region.
The volcano's very recent eruption, which happened recently and unexpectedly, caused widespread destruction.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Recent eruption, which happened recently' — 'recently' is stated twice. 'In the surrounding region' is contextually appropriate to keep as it specifies scope. B removes the redundant 'which happened recently.' A keeps both. C adds 'very' and 'unexpectedly.' D rephrases but keeps the redundancy.

Text: 'The charity provides food assistance to people living in poverty who don't have enough food to eat.'

Which revision is most effective?
to food-insecure people living in poverty
to impoverished people who lack sufficient food and don't have enough to eat
to people living in poverty who don't have enough food to eat
to people who live in poverty, are hungry, and don't have enough food to eat
Medium
Precision
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Don't have enough food to eat' largely repeats the food assistance context. 'Food-insecure people living in poverty' precisely describes the population using the standard term 'food-insecure.' B is more concise and uses appropriate technical language. A keeps the wordy phrase. C adds a list with triple redundancy. D has 'lack sufficient food and don't have enough to eat' (redundant).

Text: 'The mayor gave a speech addressing the city's current infrastructure problems that exist today.'

Which revision eliminates redundancy?
addressing the city's current infrastructure problems which are present today
addressing the city's current infrastructure problems that exist today
addressing the city's infrastructure problems
addressing the current and existing infrastructure problems of the city
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Current,' 'that exist,' and 'today' all mean 'now' — triple redundancy. B: 'addressing the city's infrastructure problems' — removes all three time indicators (the context of a speech implies the problems are current). A keeps two. C has 'current and existing.' D has 'current' and 'present today.'

Text: 'The children were given tests that evaluated their reading ability at regular, scheduled intervals.'

Which revision is most effective?
that regularly and frequently evaluated their reading ability at intervals
that evaluated their reading ability at regular, scheduled intervals
that evaluated their reading ability at intervals that were regular and scheduled
that regularly evaluated their reading ability
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Regular' and 'scheduled' overlap (scheduled implies regularity). 'At intervals' is implied by 'regularly.' B: 'that regularly evaluated their reading ability' — concise and complete. A keeps both 'regular' and 'scheduled.' C restructures but keeps the redundant pair. D adds 'frequently' (redundant with regularly).

Text: 'Solar energy is a clean, renewable, and environmentally friendly source of power.'

Which revision most effectively eliminates the redundancy?
Solar energy is a clean, renewable, and environmentally friendly source of power.
Solar energy is an environmentally friendly and clean renewable source of power.
Solar energy is a clean, renewable energy source.
Solar energy is a source of clean, renewable, environmentally friendly, and sustainable power.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Clean,' 'renewable,' and 'environmentally friendly' significantly overlap — all describe the same environmental virtue. B keeps 'clean' and 'renewable' (the most standard and distinct terms). 'Source of power' → 'energy source.' A keeps all three. C reorders but keeps both. D adds 'sustainable' (fourth synonym).

Text: 'The two experiments, while different from each other, both shared the same conclusion.'

Which revision is most effective?
while being different from one another, both of them shared the same identical conclusion
while different from each other, shared an identical conclusion that was the same
though different, both reached the same conclusion
while different from each other, both shared the same conclusion
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Different from each other' → 'different' (implied between two experiments). 'Both shared the same conclusion' → 'both reached the same conclusion' ('the same' is partially redundant since sharing implies sameness; 'reached' is more precise). B: 'though different, both reached the same conclusion.' A is the original. C adds 'one another' and 'identical.' D has 'identical conclusion that was the same' (redundant).

Passage: 'The ocean floor is largely unexplored. Scientists estimate that over 80 percent of it remains unmapped.'

Which revision most effectively combines these sentences?
With over 80 percent of its area unmapped, the ocean floor remains largely unexplored.
Scientists estimate that over 80 percent of the ocean floor remains unmapped and unexplored.
The ocean floor is largely unexplored, and scientists estimate that over 80 percent of it remains unmapped.
The ocean floor, which is largely unexplored, remains unmapped in over 80 percent of its area according to scientists.
Medium
Revision
Sentence Revision & Clarity

D begins with the striking statistic (80 percent unmapped), then delivers the conclusion (largely unexplored) — effective structure that leads with specific evidence. B repeats 'unmapped and unexplored' (redundant). A combines with 'and' but 'largely unexplored' and 'over 80 percent unmapped' are redundant. C is wordy with 'which is' and 'in over 80 percent of its area.'

Text: 'The research institute was founded for the explicit purpose of specifically investigating rare genetic disorders.'

Which revision is most concise?
was specifically founded for the explicit purpose of investigating rare genetic disorders
was founded for the purpose and goal of specifically investigating rare genetic disorders
was founded to investigate rare genetic disorders
was founded for the explicit purpose of specifically investigating rare genetic disorders
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'For the explicit purpose of specifically investigating' → 'to investigate.' Both 'explicit purpose of' and 'specifically' add no information: 'founded to investigate' states the purpose with complete clarity. B is maximally concise. A is the wordy original. C adds 'and goal.' D moves 'specifically' but keeps 'explicit purpose of.'

Text: 'Despite the fact that the road was closed, the delivery driver found an alternative route.'

Which revision is most concise?
Despite the fact that the road was closed, the delivery driver found an alternative route.
Due to the fact that the road was closed, the delivery driver found an alternative route.
Although the road was closed, the delivery driver found an alternative route.
Despite the road being closed, the delivery driver found an alternative route instead.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Despite the fact that' → 'although' (4 words → 1 word, same meaning). B: 'Although the road was closed, the delivery driver found an alternative route.' A keeps the wordy phrase. C wrongly uses 'due to the fact that' (which means because, changing the meaning). D uses 'Despite the road being closed' (acceptable but slightly awkward) and adds 'instead.'

Text: 'The pharmaceutical company's latest drug has proven to be very effective in the treatment of patients with a rare form of cancer.'

Which revision most effectively improves the sentence?
has been proven to be effective in the treatment of patients who have a rare form of cancer
has proven to be very effective in the treatment of cancer patients with a rare form of cancer
has proven to be very effective in the treatment of patients with a rare form of cancer
has proven effective in treating patients with a rare form of cancer
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Very effective' → 'effective' ('very' adds little). 'In the treatment of patients' → 'in treating patients' (shorter). B: 'has proven effective in treating patients with a rare form of cancer.' A keeps 'very' and the wordy 'in the treatment of.' C adds a redundant 'cancer patients with a rare form of cancer.' D adds 'who have' (wordy).

Text: 'The meeting room was prepared in advance before the conference began.'

Which revision eliminates the redundancy?
was prepared in advance before the conference began
was prepared ahead of time in advance before the conference began
was prepared in advance and beforehand before the conference began
was prepared before the conference began
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'In advance' and 'before the conference began' both convey the same meaning — one is sufficient. B keeps only 'before the conference began' (more specific and informative). A keeps both. C adds 'and beforehand.' D adds 'ahead of time' — triple redundancy.

Text: 'The new transportation plan was both comprehensive and thorough in its approach to solving the city's traffic problems.'

Which revision is most effective?
was both comprehensive and thorough in comprehensively solving the city's traffic problems
was comprehensive in its approach to the city's traffic problems
was both comprehensive and thorough in its approach to solving the city's traffic problems
was a thorough and comprehensive approach that comprehensively addressed the city's traffic problems
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Comprehensive' and 'thorough' are redundant when both describe an approach. 'In its approach to solving' → 'in its approach to' (the 'solving' is implied). B: 'was comprehensive in its approach to the city's traffic problems.' A keeps the redundant pair. C adds 'comprehensively' (triple). D has multiple repetitions of 'comprehensive.'

Text: 'The government's plan to improve and enhance economic growth will create jobs.'

Which revision most effectively eliminates redundancy?
to improve, enhance, and develop economic growth
to improve and enhance economic growth
to improve and enhance overall economic growth
to enhance economic growth
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity
'Improve' and 'enhance' are synonyms — redundant pair. B keeps only 'enhance.' A keeps both. C adds 'develop' (third synonym). D adds 'overall.'

Text: 'The scientists collaborated together on the project, sharing resources and knowledge.'

Which revision eliminates redundancy?
The scientists worked together collaboratively on the project, sharing resources and knowledge.
The scientists collaborated together and worked jointly on the project.
The scientists collaborated together on the project, sharing resources and knowledge.
The scientists collaborated on the project, sharing resources and knowledge.
Medium
Wordiness
Sentence Revision & Clarity

'Collaborate' already means working together — 'together' is redundant. B removes it. A keeps 'together.' C adds 'worked together collaboratively' (triple redundancy). D has 'together' and 'jointly' (still redundant).

The new alloy is far lighter than steel. ______, it withstands temperatures that would warp most metals.

Which transition best fits?
By contrast
Moreover
However
Nevertheless
Hard
Transitions
Sentence Revision & Clarity
Both sentences state advantages of the alloy, so the relationship is addition — 'Moreover.' 'However,' 'Nevertheless,' and 'By contrast' all signal contrast, which doesn't fit two stacked benefits.

A student wants to emphasize a contrast between two researchers' methods. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?

Notes: Dr. Lee relied on large-scale computer simulations. Dr. Ortiz relied on small, hand-built physical models.
Dr. Lee used simulations, and Dr. Ortiz used physical models, each producing useful data.
Both researchers contributed to the field through careful methodology.
Dr. Lee and Dr. Ortiz both studied the same problem using different tools.
Whereas Dr. Lee relied on large-scale computer simulations, Dr. Ortiz built small physical models by hand.
Challenge
Rhetorical Synthesis
Rhetorical Synthesis
The goal is to emphasize contrast. 'Whereas… ' explicitly frames the two methods against each other. The others note a difference only mildly or stress similarity, weakening the contrast.
Standard English Conventions:
Text: 'The collection of handwritten letters from the early twentieth century [___] recently been donated to the university library.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of handwritten letters from the early twentieth century.' Subject = 'collection' (singular) → has.

Text: 'The committee on environmental standards [___] voted to adopt stricter regulations on industrial emissions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Committee' is a collective noun — singular in American English. It acts as a unit → has.

Text: 'A number of studies examining the long-term effects of sleep deprivation on cognitive function [___] produced alarming results.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'A number of X' = PLURAL → have. (Contrast: 'The number of studies HAS grown' — 'the number' = singular.)

Text: 'The team of researchers, along with several graduate students, [___] presented findings at last month's conference.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Along with several graduate students' is an intervening phrase — cross it out. Subject = 'The team' (singular collective noun) → has.

Text: 'The number of species affected by climate change [___] grown dramatically since the 1980s.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The number of X' = SINGULAR → has. Cross out 'of species affected by climate change.' Subject = 'the number' → has.

Text: 'Every student, teacher, and administrator in the district [___] required to complete the new training module.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
When 'every' or 'each' precedes a compound subject joined by 'and,' the subject is still treated as SINGULAR. 'Every student, teacher, and administrator' → singular → is.

Text: 'The report, together with its supporting appendices, [___] submitted to the board last Friday.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Together with its supporting appendices' is an intervening phrase (cross it out). Subject = 'The report' (singular) → was.

Text: 'The policy changes announced by the administration [___] sparked widespread debate among educators.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out the intervening phrase 'announced by the administration.' Subject = 'changes' (plural) → have.

Text: 'There [___] a series of unresolved questions about the long-term safety of the compound.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Inverted sentence — find the subject after 'There ___.' Subject = 'a series' (singular collective noun) → is. 'A series of X' = singular.

Text: 'The jury [___] still deliberating when the judge called for a recess.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Jury' = collective noun, singular in American English → was. The jury acts as a unified body.

Text: 'Neither the proposed budget nor the alternative plans [___] received sufficient support from the full council.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither...nor': verb agrees with the CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'plans' (plural) → have.

Text: 'The box of vintage photographs [___] discovered in the attic when the family was renovating.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of vintage photographs.' Subject = 'The box' (singular) → was.

Text: 'Each of the participating countries [___] agreed to reduce carbon emissions by at least 30 percent by 2030.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Each' is always SINGULAR regardless of the following noun. Cross out 'of the participating countries.' Subject = 'each' → has.

Text: 'The evidence gathered from multiple independent studies [___] overwhelmingly supports the conclusion.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'gathered from multiple independent studies.' Subject = 'evidence' (singular, uncountable) → has.

Text: 'There [___] many examples throughout history of scientific consensus being overturned by new evidence.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Subject after 'there' = 'many examples' (plural) → are. 'Many' always indicates plural.

Text: 'The group of scientists who conducted the experiment [___] published their findings in a peer-reviewed journal.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of scientists who conducted the experiment.' Subject = 'The group' (singular collective) → has.

Text: 'Neither the director nor the board members [___] aware of the financial discrepancies before the audit.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither...nor': verb agrees with the CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'board members' (plural) → were.

Text: 'The list of ingredients required for the recipe [___] available on the company's website.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of ingredients required for the recipe.' Subject = 'The list' (singular) → is.

Text: 'Several of the artifacts discovered at the archaeological site [___] been sent to the national museum for analysis.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Several' is ALWAYS PLURAL → have. Cross out 'of the artifacts discovered at the archaeological site.'

Text: 'The presence of microplastics in drinking water sources around the world [___] alarmed public health officials.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of microplastics in drinking water sources around the world.' Subject = 'The presence' (singular) → has.

Text: 'Both the CEO and the board [___] approved the merger, though under very different conditions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Both X and Y' = ALWAYS PLURAL → have. 'Both' explicitly signals two separate parties.

Text: 'The faculty, including several adjunct instructors, [___] voted against the proposed curriculum changes.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Including several adjunct instructors' is an intervening phrase — cross it out. Subject = 'The faculty' (singular collective noun) → has.

Text: 'There [___] no simple explanation for why the experiment produced inconsistent results across different conditions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Text: 'One of the factors that [___] contributed most significantly to the company's growth is its investment in employee training.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'That' refers to 'factors' (plural). 'One of the factors that ___' → 'that' refers to 'factors' (plural) → have. (If it were 'the only one of the factors that,' the answer would be 'has.')

Text: 'The number of hours devoted to standardized test preparation in public schools [___] increased steadily since the 1990s.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The number of X' = SINGULAR → has. Cross out the long intervening phrase.

Text: 'The mayor, as well as several city council members, [___] expected to attend the opening ceremony.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'As well as several city council members' is an intervening phrase — cross it out. Subject = 'The mayor' (singular) → is.

Text: 'All of the data collected during the first phase of the study [___] now been reviewed by an independent panel.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'All' is flexible — agree with the noun in 'of X.' Here: 'data' is singular (uncountable) → has. Compare: 'All of the samples HAVE been reviewed' (samples = plural).

Text: 'A team of engineers working on the next generation of electric vehicles [___] achieved a significant breakthrough in battery efficiency.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of engineers working on the next generation of electric vehicles.' Subject = 'A team' (singular collective noun) → has.

Text: 'Neither rain, wind, nor extreme heat [___] capable of stopping the volunteers from completing the habitat restoration.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither X, Y, nor Z': verb agrees with the LAST/CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'extreme heat' (singular) → is.

Text: 'The series of lectures on contemporary philosophy [___] proved to be far more popular than the organizers expected.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of lectures on contemporary philosophy.' Subject = 'The series' (singular) → has. 'Series' is always singular.

Text: 'Everyone who attended the conference [___] asked to complete a brief feedback survey before leaving.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Everyone' is ALWAYS SINGULAR → was. Cross out 'who attended the conference.'

Text: 'Each of the candidates [___] required to submit a portfolio demonstrating their design skills.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Each' is ALWAYS SINGULAR → is. The 'of the candidates' phrase doesn't change this.

Text: 'Some of the funding allocated for infrastructure improvements [___] redirected toward emergency relief.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Some' is flexible. 'Some of the funding' → 'funding' is singular (uncountable) → was.

Text: 'None of the participants [___] informed about the true purpose of the study until after it concluded.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'None of X': when the 'of' noun is plural (participants), modern standard English accepts both singular and plural, but 'were' is the most natural and is accepted on the SAT when 'none' refers to a plural noun.

Text: 'The scientist is one of the researchers who [___] dedicated decades to studying deep-sea biodiversity.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'One of the researchers who' → 'who' refers to 'researchers' (plural). Several researchers have dedicated decades. Plural → have.

Text: 'Several findings from the survey [___] questioned the validity of the commonly accepted model.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Several' is ALWAYS PLURAL → have. 'Several findings' = plural.

Text: 'Not only the students but also the professor [___] surprised by the test results.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Not only X but also Y': verb agrees with the CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'the professor' (singular) → was.

Text: 'Either of the two approaches [___] likely to yield positive results in the long term.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Either' as a subject (without 'or') = SINGULAR → is. Cross out 'of the two approaches.'

Text: 'Most of the ocean floor [___] never been directly observed by humans.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Most' is flexible. 'Most of the ocean floor' → 'floor' is singular (uncountable) → has.

Text: 'The band, along with their manager and two assistants, [___] already boarded the tour bus when the delay was announced.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Along with their manager and two assistants' = intervening phrase. Subject = 'The band' (singular collective) → had.

Text: 'None of the proposed solutions [___] proven to be entirely effective in practice.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'None of the solutions' — 'solutions' is plural. In this context 'none' = 'not any of them' → plural → have.

Text: 'There [___] a wide variety of strategies available to investors seeking to manage portfolio risk.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Inverted sentence — subject after 'There' = 'a wide variety.' 'A variety' = singular (like 'a number') → is.

Text: 'Everybody in the study groups, regardless of prior knowledge, [___] given the same materials.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Everybody' = ALWAYS SINGULAR. 'Regardless of prior knowledge' = intervening phrase. Subject = 'everybody' → was.

Text: 'Many of the assumptions underlying the original model [___] now been shown to be incorrect.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Many' = ALWAYS PLURAL → have. 'Many of the assumptions' = plural.

Text: 'She is the only one of the candidates who [___] proposed a detailed policy framework for addressing housing affordability.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'The only one of the candidates who' → 'who' refers to 'the only one' (singular) — exactly one person proposed the framework. Singular → has. Contrast: 'one of the candidates who HAVE proposed' (plural — several candidates have proposed).

Text: 'Either the new policy or the proposed amendments [___] sufficient to address the current regulatory gaps.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Either X or Y': verb agrees with CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'the proposed amendments' (plural) → are.

Text: 'Neither of the two leading theories [___] fully account for all the observed phenomena.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither' as a subject (without 'nor') = SINGULAR → does. 'Neither of the two theories does fully account...'

Text: 'A series of administrative errors made during the initial enrollment process [___] contributed to the confusion.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of administrative errors made during the initial enrollment process.' Subject = 'A series' (singular) → has.

Text: 'Some of the most compelling arguments against the proposal [___] raised by economists at the conference.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Some of the arguments' → 'arguments' is plural → were.

Text: 'The orchestra, despite having some members miss rehearsals, [___] delivered a flawless performance.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Despite having some members miss rehearsals' = intervening phrase. Subject = 'The orchestra' (singular collective) → has.

Text: 'No one among the hundreds of spectators who witnessed the incident [___] come forward with additional information.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'No one' = ALWAYS SINGULAR → has. 'Among the hundreds of spectators who witnessed the incident' = intervening phrase.

Text: 'Both the experimental data and the theoretical framework [___] consistent with the hypothesis.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Both X and Y' = ALWAYS PLURAL → are.

Text: 'The majority of funding for public universities [___] come from state allocations and tuition revenue.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The majority of X': 'funding' = singular (uncountable) → has. Compare: 'The majority of funds HAVE come from...' (funds = plural).

Text: 'Anyone who [___] questions about the application process should contact the admissions office directly.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Anyone' = ALWAYS SINGULAR → has. The relative clause 'who has questions' correctly uses singular.

Text: 'The wealth of literary traditions found across the continent [___] been largely overlooked by mainstream academic publishers.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of literary traditions found across the continent.' Subject = 'The wealth' (singular) → has.

Text: 'Either the witnesses or the defendant [___] providing false information to the court.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Either X or Y': verb agrees with CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'the defendant' (singular) → is.

Text: 'Few of the proposals submitted during the public comment period [___] ultimately incorporated into the final plan.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Few' = ALWAYS PLURAL → were. 'Few of the proposals' = plural.

Text: 'The set of instructions provided with the equipment [___] confusing and incomplete, according to most users.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Cross out 'of instructions provided with the equipment.' Subject = 'The set' (singular) → is.

Text: 'All of the progress made over the past decade [___] now threatened by the proposed regulatory rollbacks.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'All' is flexible. 'All of the progress' → 'progress' is singular (uncountable) → is.

Text: 'The professor, in addition to several visiting scholars, [___] expected to contribute a chapter to the anthology.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'In addition to several visiting scholars' = intervening phrase. Subject = 'The professor' (singular) → is.

Text: 'The government announced [___] intention to reform the tax code before the end of the fiscal year.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The government' is a singular collective noun → 'its.' A (their) treats it as plural.

Text: 'Each candidate must prepare [___] own statement of purpose before the interview.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Each' = singular. In formal written English, 'each candidate' takes 'his or her.' C is correct.

Text: 'The research team, frustrated by the lack of funding, decided to publish [___] preliminary findings independently.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Research team' is a collective noun acting as a unit → singular → 'its.' But as members sharing intellectual agency, 'their' is also increasingly accepted. In this context — 'publish findings' as a unified act — B (its) is more formally precise.

Text: 'The corporation restructured [___] operations to reduce overhead costs in the wake of declining revenues.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The corporation' = singular → 'its.' A (their) incorrectly treats it as plural.

Text: 'Neither the professor nor the students were satisfied with [___] performance on the first exam.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither X nor Y': pronoun agrees with CLOSEST antecedent. Closest = 'the students' (plural) → 'their.' C is correct.

Text: 'Everyone on the expedition was asked to document [___] observations in a standardized field journal.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Everyone' = singular indefinite pronoun. Formal SAT convention: 'his or her.' C is correct. A (their) is informal/contemporary but the SAT still tests the formal singular form for indefinite pronouns.

Text: 'The company and [___] subsidiary both reported strong earnings for the third quarter.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The company' is singular. 'Its subsidiary' — the subsidiary belongs to the singular company → 'its.' A is correct.

Text: 'No one should be forced to compromise [___] principles simply to advance a career.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'No one' = SINGULAR indefinite pronoun → 'his or her' in formal register. C is correct.

Text: 'The committee published [___] annual report outlining the progress made toward achieving sustainability goals.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The committee' = singular collective noun → 'its.' D is correct. A (their) is incorrect for a singular noun. B (it's) = 'it is' — wrong word.

Text: 'Both the director and the lead actor acknowledged [___] debt to the playwright's original vision.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Both X and Y' = plural → 'their.' C is correct. They share a collective debt.

Text: 'The university updated [___] admissions policy to consider a wider range of socioeconomic factors.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The university' = singular → 'its.' C is correct. A (their) is plural. B (it's) = 'it is.'

Text: 'Each country in the alliance pledged to increase [___] defense budget by two percent over the next decade.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Each country' — 'each' modifies 'country' (singular) → 'its.' B is correct. Though 'their' is increasingly used informally, 'its' is more formally precise for a singular noun.

Text: 'Neither of the lead researchers was willing to retract [___] published findings without further evidence.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither of the lead researchers' — 'neither' is singular → 'his or her.' B is correct.

Text: 'The board of directors voted to approve the merger despite [___] concerns about the valuation.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The board of directors' = singular collective noun → 'its.' A is correct. The board as a unified body has 'its' concerns.

Text: 'Every scientist and engineer on the project was asked to submit [___] individual assessment by Friday.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Every X and Y' — 'every' makes a compound subject singular → 'his or her.' C is correct.

Text: 'The school district and [___] neighboring districts collaborated on a joint initiative to address learning gaps.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The school district' = singular → 'its neighboring districts.' C is correct.

Text: 'Anyone who hopes to succeed in this field must be willing to question [___] assumptions regularly.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Anyone' = SINGULAR indefinite pronoun → 'his or her' in formal register. C is correct.

Text: 'The jury returned [___] verdict after six days of deliberation, finding the defendant not guilty on all counts.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The jury' = singular collective noun → 'its verdict.' C is correct.

Text: 'Neither the mayor nor the council members shared [___] full reasoning with the press.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither X nor Y': pronoun agrees with CLOSEST antecedent. Closest = 'council members' (plural) → 'their.' C is correct.

Text: 'The nonprofit organization dedicated all of [___] resources to providing educational support for underserved youth.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The nonprofit organization' = singular → 'its.' C is correct.

Text: 'Each of the competing firms submitted [___] proposal before the deadline set by the contracting agency.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Each' is singular. The antecedent is 'each of the competing firms' — 'firms' are organizations, not people → 'its' (not 'his or her'). B is correct.

Text: 'The orchestra performed [___] final concert of the season to a sold-out audience.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The orchestra' = singular collective noun → 'its.' C is correct.

Text: 'Somebody left [___] laptop on the conference table after the meeting concluded.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Somebody' = SINGULAR indefinite → 'his or her.' C is correct in formal written English.

Text: 'The government must reassess [___] approach to immigration policy in light of the changing economic conditions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Text: 'The firm announced that [___] would begin hiring again once market conditions improved.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The firm' = singular → 'it.' B is correct. A (they) incorrectly treats a singular organization as plural.

Text: 'Neither the lead researcher nor her colleagues were able to replicate [___] original findings.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither X nor Y': pronoun agrees with CLOSEST antecedent. Closest = 'colleagues' (plural) → 'their.' D is correct.

Text: 'Every student in the advanced placement program must complete [___] thesis by the end of the spring semester.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Every student' — 'every' makes subject singular. Students are people → 'his or her.' D is correct.

Text: 'The startup and [___] parent company have been in discussions about a potential acquisition.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The startup' = singular → 'its parent company.' C is correct.

Text: 'No student should submit [___] final paper without proofreading it at least twice.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'No student' — 'no' makes the subject singular. Students are people → 'his or her.' C is correct in formal academic writing.

Text: 'The panel of reviewers submitted [___] recommendations to the board after a thorough evaluation of all applications.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Panel of reviewers' — when the members act as individuals (each contributed recommendations), 'their' is appropriate. The panel members collectively wrote recommendations as individuals. B (their) is most natural here.

Text: 'The prize was awarded to the scientist [___] research on gene editing had produced the most significant breakthroughs.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

The blank precedes a noun ('research') — this calls for the POSSESSIVE 'whose.' 'Whose research' = the scientist's research. C is correct. A (whom) is an object pronoun. B (which) is for non-human antecedents. D (who's) = 'who is.'

Text: 'The selection committee will choose [___] it believes is most qualified for the position.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

The clause after the blank is 'it believes ___ is most qualified' — test: 'it believes HE/HIM is most qualified' → 'he is most qualified' (subject) → WHO. But it's 'whoever' because it's the subject of the entire embedded clause that functions as the object of 'will choose.' D (whoever) is correct.

Text: 'The patient [___] the doctor recommended for the experimental treatment was carefully screened.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Test: 'the doctor recommended HIM/HER for the treatment' (the patient is the object of 'recommended') → object → WHOM. C is correct.

Text: 'The conflict between her supervisor and [___] made it difficult for her to focus on the project.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Between' is a preposition → object pronoun. Test: remove 'her supervisor and' → 'between [she/him]' → 'between him' sounds right. C (him) is correct.

Text: 'The lead investigator, [___] had reviewed hundreds of similar cases, recognized the pattern immediately.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Test: '[she/her] had reviewed hundreds of cases' → 'she had reviewed' (subject) → WHO. B is correct.

Text: 'Between you and [___], the proposed budget is far too optimistic given current market conditions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Between' is a preposition → object pronouns. 'Between you and me.' C is correct. A (I) is a subject pronoun — incorrect after prepositions. B (myself) is reflexive.

Text: 'The editors decided that [___] would publish the full report, not just the executive summary.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The editors' = plural → 'they.' C is correct. A (one) is impersonal. B (it) is singular.

Text: 'The voters [___] the candidate had targeted for outreach ultimately supported a different nominee.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Test: 'the candidate had targeted THEM for outreach' (voters are the object of 'targeted') → object → WHOM. B is correct.

Text: 'It was she and [___] who first proposed the compromise that ended the months-long standoff.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'She and ___' are the subject of the sentence (they proposed). Subject pronoun → 'he.' B is correct. A (him) is an object pronoun. When the pronouns are after 'it was,' they are subject complements — still use subject pronouns.

Text: 'The biologist [___] discovered the enzyme has since published follow-up research confirming the original findings.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Test: '[she/her] discovered the enzyme' → 'she discovered' (subject) → WHO. C is correct.

Passage: 'Historians have studied the French Revolution extensively. It transformed European society.'

The pronoun 'it' in the second sentence is ambiguous — it could refer to either historians' study or the French Revolution. Which revision of the second sentence most clearly eliminates the ambiguity?
The French Revolution transformed European society.

B replaces the ambiguous 'it' with the specific noun 'the French Revolution,' making the reference unambiguous. A keeps the ambiguous pronoun. C changes meaning (now refers to historians' study). D introduces another ambiguous pronoun.

Text: 'The professor gave the students [___] notes before the exam.'

The antecedent of the pronoun is ambiguous. Which revision best eliminates the ambiguity?
The professor returned the students' notes before the exam.
The professor gave the students their notes before the exam.
The professor gave the students her notes before the exam.
The professor gave the students some notes before the exam.

'[___] notes' is ambiguous — whose notes? The professor's or the students'? A (her notes) specifies the professor's notes, eliminating ambiguity. B (their notes) would mean the students' own notes, which changes meaning. C (some notes) avoids the pronoun but loses specificity about ownership. D changes the verb significantly.

Text: 'The manager told the employee that [___] needed to revise the report before submitting it.'

The pronoun is ambiguous. Which revision best clarifies meaning?
The manager told the employee that she needed to revise the report before submitting it.
The manager told the employee they needed to revise the report.
The manager, telling the employee, needed to revise the report before submitting it.
The manager told the employee that the report needed revision before submission.

'That [___] needed to revise' is ambiguous — did the manager or the employee need to revise? B restructures to eliminate the pronoun and state the meaning directly: 'the report needed revision.' A (she) makes an assumption about who needs to revise. D uses 'they' which is still ambiguous.

Text: 'The city will expand [___] public transit system over the next five years.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Text: 'The pharmaceutical company reported that [___] new drug had passed all phase-three clinical trials.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The pharmaceutical company' = singular → 'its.' C is correct.

Text: 'The researcher presented the data to the statistician and then asked [___] to verify the calculations.'

The antecedent of the pronoun 'them' is ambiguous. Which revision best clarifies the sentence?
The researcher presented the data to the statistician and then asked them to verify the calculations.
The researcher presented the data to the statistician and then asked the statistician to verify the calculations.
The researcher asked the statistician, presenting data, to verify the calculations.
The researcher, presenting data, asked for verification of calculations.
'Asked them' is ambiguous — did the researcher ask the statistician, or ask multiple people? B replaces 'them' with 'the statistician,' making the reference clear. A keeps the ambiguous pronoun.

Text: 'The physicist [___] theory revolutionized our understanding of space and time received the Nobel Prize in 1921.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
The blank precedes 'theory' (a noun) — this requires the POSSESSIVE 'whose.' 'The physicist whose theory...' C is correct.

Text: 'The award committee selected [___] they considered the most deserving candidate.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

The clause structure: 'they considered [him/her] the most deserving' — object of 'considered' → 'whomever.' D is correct. 'Whomever' is used because it begins a noun clause that functions as the object of 'selected,' and within that clause, the pronoun is also an object.

Text: 'The debate was won by [___] argued most effectively for meaningful criminal justice reform.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'By' is a preposition — you might think it needs 'whomever.' But test: the clause '[he/him] argued most effectively' → 'he argued' (subject) → who. The whole clause 'whoever argued most effectively' is the object of 'by,' but within the clause, the pronoun is the subject → whoever. B is correct.

Text: 'The scholarship was established for students [___] families cannot afford full tuition.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Blank precedes 'families' (a noun) → need POSSESSIVE → 'whose.' 'Students whose families cannot afford...' C is correct.

Text: 'The new policy pleased both the director and [___].'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'The new policy pleased [the director and ___].' Test by removing 'the director and': 'pleased [I/me]' → 'pleased me' (object of 'pleased') → object pronoun → 'me.' C is correct. A and B are subject pronouns. D (myself) is reflexive.

Text: 'The award was presented to [___] had demonstrated the greatest commitment to community service.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

The clause 'whoever had demonstrated...' — test: '[he/him] had demonstrated' → 'he had demonstrated' (subject) → 'whoever.' The entire clause 'whoever had demonstrated the greatest commitment' is the object of 'to,' but within the clause, the pronoun is the subject → whoever. C is correct.

Text: 'It was the volunteers and [___] who organized the entire fundraising event from start to finish.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The volunteers and ___' are the SUBJECT of the sentence (they organized). Subject pronoun → 'I.' A is correct. Think: 'It was [we] who organized' → we = subject form → I for singular component.

Text: 'The professor, [___] lectures had inspired a generation of environmental scientists, retired after 35 years.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Blank precedes 'lectures' (a noun) → POSSESSIVE → 'whose.' 'The professor, whose lectures had inspired...' C is correct.

Text: 'The senator [___] colleagues had voted against the bill decided to reconsider her position.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Blank precedes 'colleagues' (a noun) → POSSESSIVE → 'whose.' 'The senator whose colleagues had voted against...' B is correct.

Text: 'Please direct all complaints to the manager or [___].'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'To the manager or ___' — 'to' is a preposition → object pronoun. Test: remove 'the manager or': 'to [I/me]' → 'to me.' C (me) is correct.

Text: 'The foundation awarded grants to organizations [___] missions aligned with its priorities.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Blank precedes 'missions' (a noun belonging to the organizations) → POSSESSIVE → 'whose.' 'Organizations whose missions aligned...' C is correct.

Passage: 'When the city council reviewed the developer's proposal, they approved it with minor modifications.'

The pronoun 'it' could be ambiguous. In this passage, 'it' most clearly refers to

In context, 'it' follows 'reviewed the developer's proposal' and 'they approved it' — the most recent and logical antecedent is 'the developer's proposal.' C is correct. The city council (A) reviewed it but can't approve itself. The developer (B) is a person. The modifications (D) come after.

Text: 'The historian argued with the journalist, but in the end [___] changed [___] position on the matter.'

A student wants to revise the sentence to eliminate the ambiguity in both pronouns. Which revision is clearest?
The historian changed her position after arguing.
The historian argued with the journalist, but in the end she changed her position.
The historian argued with the journalist, but the historian ultimately changed her position.
After arguing with the journalist, the historian changed positions.

C eliminates both ambiguous pronouns by restructuring: 'the historian' is now clearly the subject throughout, and no pronouns remain for the 'who changed' question. B clarifies who changed position ('the historian') but 'her' is still potentially ambiguous. A uses 'she' and 'her' — still ambiguous since both historian and journalist could be female. D is clear and concise.

Text: 'The research team credited both the lead scientist and [___] for the groundbreaking discovery.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Credited [the lead scientist and ___].' Test: remove 'the lead scientist and' → 'credited [I/him]' → 'credited him' (object of 'credited') → object pronoun → 'him.' C is correct.

Text: 'The experiment produced unexpected results[___] the team immediately redesigned the protocol.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them.

Text: 'The bridge, which was built in 1923[___] has withstood numerous earthquakes without significant structural damage.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Which was built in 1923' is a NONRESTRICTIVE clause — it adds information but doesn't identify which bridge. Nonrestrictive elements need commas on BOTH sides. The opening comma is present; a closing comma is needed here. A (,) is correct.

Text: 'After carefully analyzing three years of climate data[___] the researchers concluded that temperatures had risen faster than projected.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
An introductory participial phrase ('After carefully analyzing...') must be followed by a comma before the main clause. C (,) is correct.

Text: 'The students who complete all required coursework[___] will be eligible to graduate in May.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Who complete all required coursework' is RESTRICTIVE — it identifies WHICH students (not all students, only those who complete coursework). No commas around restrictive clauses. B (no punctuation) is correct.

Text: 'The concert was sold out[___] many fans waited outside hoping to buy last-minute tickets.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Two independent clauses ('The concert was sold out' / 'many fans waited outside...'). A comma alone (A) creates a comma splice. B adds 'and' with a comma — grammatically correct. C (semicolon) is also correct. D (no punctuation) creates a run-on. Both B and C work; on the SAT, C is preferred when no conjunction is given. C is best.

Text: 'The novel, written over a period of ten years[___] draws on the author's experiences living in three different countries.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Written over a period of ten years' is a nonrestrictive participial phrase providing extra information about the novel. It needs commas on BOTH sides. The opening comma is already there; a closing comma is needed. B (,) is correct.

Text: 'Scientists have long studied the effects of sleep deprivation[___] researchers continue to discover new neurological consequences.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Two independent clauses. A comma alone = comma splice (A wrong). C (semicolon) correctly joins two independent clauses. B adds 'and' with a comma — also grammatically correct, but since we're choosing from four options, C (semicolon) is the clean correct punctuation choice.

Text: 'The park features hiking trails, a botanical garden[___] and a small amphitheater for outdoor performances.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Series of three items: 'hiking trails, a botanical garden, and a small amphitheater.' Standard comma before 'and' in a series (Oxford comma). C (,) is correct. A semicolon would only be needed if the items had internal commas.

Text: 'The proposal was rejected[___] the board felt it lacked sufficient financial justification.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
"Because" makes the second clause dependent: "rejected because the board felt..." C is natural and correct.

Text: 'The architect designed the museum[___] but the city lacked funding to build it for another decade.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses joined by 'but' (FANBOYS) require a comma before 'but.' C (,) is correct.

Text: 'Dr. Chen, the lead researcher on the project[___] presented her findings at the international conference.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The lead researcher on the project' is a NONRESTRICTIVE appositive (renames Dr. Chen). It needs commas on both sides. The opening comma is present; a closing comma is needed. C (,) is correct.

Text: 'Although the weather forecast predicted rain[___] the outdoor ceremony proceeded as planned.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Although the weather forecast predicted rain' is an introductory dependent clause. Must be followed by a comma before the main clause. C (,) is correct.

Text: 'The legislation was praised by economists[___] criticized by labor unions, and debated extensively in the press.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
This is a series: 'praised by economists, criticized by labor unions, and debated...' The comma after 'economists' is needed to separate the first and second items in the series. B (,) is correct.

Text: 'The students submitted their papers[___] the professor immediately noticed the high quality of the arguments.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Two independent clauses. A comma alone = comma splice. C (semicolon) correctly joins them. B would also work but no 'and' is provided separately — looking at options, B gives ', and' which is also correct. Both B and C work; C is the pure punctuation-only fix.

Text: 'The company hired three specialists from Boston, Massachusetts[___] Chicago, Illinois[___] and Seattle, Washington.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complex list with city-state pairs (internal commas) → use semicolons as separators: 'Boston, Massachusetts; Chicago, Illinois; and Seattle, Washington.' C (semicolons in both positions) is correct.

Text: 'The film received mixed reviews[___] it became one of the highest-grossing movies of the year.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

The two clauses contrast (mixed reviews YET high grossing). B ('; nevertheless,') correctly uses conjunctive adverb pattern: semicolon before 'nevertheless,' comma after. A (comma alone) = comma splice. C changes the meaning. D = run-on.

Text: 'The lake[___] which has been protected since 1973[___] supports dozens of endangered species.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Which has been protected since 1973' is NONRESTRICTIVE (extra info about a specific lake) → commas on BOTH sides: 'The lake, which has been protected since 1973, supports...' B (comma both sides) is correct.

Text: 'To succeed in this field, candidates must demonstrate strong analytical skills, effective communication[___] and the ability to work collaboratively under pressure.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Three items in a series: 'strong analytical skills, effective communication, and the ability...' Standard Oxford comma before 'and.' B (,) is correct. A semicolon would only be used if list items had internal commas.

Text: 'The researcher who published the controversial paper[___] later retracted her conclusions after the study could not be replicated.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Who published the controversial paper' is RESTRICTIVE — it identifies WHICH researcher. No commas. B (no punctuation) is correct.

Text: 'The company's profits increased significantly last quarter[___] the CEO attributed this success to the new marketing strategy.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Two independent clauses. D (semicolon alone) correctly joins them. A = comma splice. B = comma + 'and' is grammatically correct but not listed cleanly. C (semicolon + and) = wrong, never use semicolon before FANBOYS. D is the clean correct answer.

Text: 'Before the 20th century, most people believed the atom was indivisible[___] Ernest Rutherford's gold foil experiment changed everything.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Two independent clauses with contrast implied (belief THEN discovery). C (semicolon) correctly joins them. A = comma splice. B ('; however,') adds 'however' which is fine logically but adds a word. C is the cleanest punctuation choice without changing words.

Text: 'The documentary explores the lives of three pioneering scientists[___] Marie Curie, Rosalind Franklin, and Lise Meitner.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

The sentence introduces a list that explains 'three pioneering scientists.' A colon introduces a list after a complete independent clause. D (:) is correct. (Note: this is a Day 14 topic — colons — but appears here as a comparison question.) Wait — the options here should only test comma vs. semicolon for Day 13. Let me reconsider: for this question on Day 13, D (colon) is the correct answer even though it's technically Day 14 material. The SAT mixes punctuation.

Text: 'The athlete trained for twelve hours a day[___] even so, she struggled to qualify for the national team.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Even so' is a conjunctive adverb. Pattern: semicolon before + comma after. C ('; even so,') is correct. A (comma alone before 'even so') = comma splice. D works too (period + new sentence) but C is the full correct pattern.

Text: 'The report, which analyzed data from fifty countries[___] found no significant correlation between economic growth and happiness.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Which analyzed data from fifty countries' is NONRESTRICTIVE (there is one report being discussed). Needs commas on BOTH sides. Opening comma is present; closing comma needed. B (,) is correct.

Text: 'In 1928 Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin[___] his finding would eventually save hundreds of millions of lives.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them. A = comma splice. B adds a conjunction. The clean punctuation-only fix is C.

Text: 'The final exam covered topics from the entire semester[___] including thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and materials science.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Including thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and materials science' is NOT an independent clause — it's an introductory phrase. A semicolon requires independent clauses on both sides. B (,) or D (—) are both possible; a comma is the standard choice before a non-essential list-introducing phrase. B is correct.

Text: 'The engineers tested the prototype extensively[___] they were satisfied with the results before proceeding to mass production.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses with a cause-effect relationship. C (semicolon) cleanly joins them. B ('; therefore,') also works logically but adds the word 'therefore.' C is the minimal correct fix.

Text: 'Every year, the foundation awards grants to researchers studying neuroscience[___] cancer biology[___] and climate science.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Simple series: 'neuroscience, cancer biology, and climate science' — no items have internal commas, so standard commas are used. A (comma and comma) gives: 'neuroscience, cancer biology, and climate science.' Correct.

Text: 'The prime minister announced new economic policies[___] the opposition party immediately denounced them as insufficient.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them without adding a conjunction. A = comma splice. B adds 'and.' The clean fix is C.

Text: 'Having reviewed all the evidence[___] the jury reached its verdict in less than two hours.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Having reviewed all the evidence' is an introductory participial phrase. Must be followed by a comma before the main clause. C (,) is correct.

Text: 'The senator, a former professor of economics[___] argued that the proposed tax cuts would disproportionately benefit the wealthy.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'A former professor of economics' is a NONRESTRICTIVE appositive. Needs commas on both sides. Opening comma is present; closing comma required. C (,) is correct.

Text: 'The discovery challenged long-held assumptions about evolution[___] furthermore, it suggested an entirely new mechanism for genetic adaptation.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Furthermore' is a conjunctive adverb. Pattern: [clause]; furthermore, [clause]. B is correct. A (comma before furthermore) = comma splice. C (comma furthermore without the semicolon) = comma splice.

Text: 'Students who take at least one statistics course[___] tend to perform better on data interpretation sections of standardized tests.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Who take at least one statistics course' is RESTRICTIVE — it identifies which students. No commas. B (no punctuation) is correct.

Text: 'The company invested heavily in renewable energy[___] it saw this as both an ethical imperative and a long-term financial opportunity.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them. A = comma splice. B (', for') uses 'for' as FANBOYS meaning 'because' — also grammatically correct, but the semicolon (C) is the clean punctuation-only fix.

Text: 'The painting, which sold for $45 million at auction[___] had been missing for over 60 years.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Which sold for $45 million at auction' is nonrestrictive. Opening comma is present; closing comma needed. C (,) is correct.

Text: 'Researchers collected soil samples from three regions[___] the Sahara Desert, the Amazon Basin, and the Siberian tundra.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
The sentence introduces a list after a complete clause. A colon is standard before a list that explains the preceding noun. D (:) is correct. (This tests the colon, previewing Day 14.)

Text: 'The results were unexpected[___] the scientists remained cautiously optimistic.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) cleanly joins them. A = comma splice. B ('; yet,') adds 'yet' — grammatically possible but adds a word. The minimal correct fix is C.

Text: 'Under the new regulations, companies must disclose environmental impact, labor practices[___] and supply chain transparency.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Three items in a series, none with internal commas: 'environmental impact, labor practices, and supply chain transparency.' Oxford comma before 'and.' B (,) is correct.

Text: 'The expedition team included linguists from Paris, France[___] marine biologists from Tokyo, Japan[___] and geologists from Cape Town, South Africa.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complex list with city-state/city-country pairs (internal commas). Use semicolons as separators: 'Paris, France; Tokyo, Japan; and Cape Town, South Africa.' B is correct.

Text: 'Although the medication showed promise in early trials[___] serious side effects were discovered during phase three testing.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Introductory dependent clause ('Although...trials') must be followed by a comma. C (,) is correct.

Text: 'The novelist worked on the manuscript for seven years[___] she revised it completely three times before submitting it to publishers.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them. A = comma splice. B ('; and') incorrectly uses semicolon before FANBOYS. D = run-on.

Text: 'The school's principal, Dr. Martinez[___] introduced several innovative programs during her tenure.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Dr. Martinez' is a NONRESTRICTIVE appositive (renames 'the school's principal'). Needs commas on both sides. Opening comma is present; closing comma required. B (,) is correct.

Text: 'The data was collected over three decades[___] making it one of the most comprehensive studies of its kind.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Making it one of the most comprehensive studies' is a participial phrase (not an independent clause). A semicolon requires independent clauses. B (,) correctly uses a comma before the participial phrase that modifies the clause.

Text: 'Climate change threatens ecosystems worldwide[___] scientists urge immediate, coordinated global action.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Two independent clauses. D (semicolon) cleanly joins them. A = comma splice. B and C add conjunctive adverbs — grammatically correct but they add words not in the original. D is the minimal correct fix.

Text: 'Researchers have found that sleep deprivation impairs cognitive function, emotional regulation[___] and physical health.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Series of three items. Oxford comma before 'and.' B (,) is correct. Items have no internal commas, so no semicolons needed.

Text: 'The museum displayed artifacts from ancient Egypt, including tools, pottery[___] and ceremonial objects.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Simple series: 'tools, pottery, and ceremonial objects.' No internal commas in items. Standard comma before 'and.' B (,) is correct.

Text: 'To qualify for the scholarship, applicants must submit a transcript, two letters of recommendation[___] and a personal statement.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Series: 'a transcript, two letters of recommendation, and a personal statement.' Oxford comma before 'and.' B (,) is correct.

Text: 'The satellite successfully entered orbit[___] however, communication was lost within 24 hours of launch.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'However' is a conjunctive adverb. Pattern: [clause]; however, [clause]. C ('; however,') is correct — semicolon before, comma after. A = comma splice. B omits the comma after 'however.' D has only a comma before 'however' = comma splice.

Text: 'The policy was controversial among economists[___] it received widespread public support.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses showing contrast. C (semicolon) is the minimal correct fix. B adds 'nevertheless' — also correct logically. C is cleaner.

Text: 'The proposal outlined three key initiatives[___] reducing carbon emissions, expanding renewable energy, and improving public transportation.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
A colon introduces a list that explains/specifies the preceding noun phrase. The clause 'The proposal outlined three key initiatives' is complete. D (:) is correct.

Text: 'The chef, who trained in Paris for five years[___] opened her own restaurant in New York City.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Who trained in Paris for five years' is NONRESTRICTIVE. Opening comma is present; closing comma required. B (,) is correct.

Text: 'Several scientists disputed the findings[___] they argued that the methodology was fundamentally flawed.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them. A = comma splice.

Text: 'The training program is open to teachers, administrators[___] and curriculum specialists from any public school.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Series of three items without internal commas. B (,) is correct.

Text: 'Throughout her career, she published over 40 papers, trained more than 200 graduate students[___] and received six major scientific awards.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Series of three items. Oxford comma before 'and.' B (,) is correct.

Text: 'The government approved the new infrastructure bill[___] construction is expected to begin next spring.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them. A = comma splice.

Text: 'Despite receiving extensive criticism[___] the director refused to alter the film's ending.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Introductory prepositional phrase ('Despite receiving extensive criticism') needs a comma before the main clause. C (,) is correct.

Text: 'The vaccine was approved for emergency use[___] only after passing all three phases of clinical trials.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Only after passing all three phases of clinical trials' is a restrictive adverbial phrase — it specifies when the vaccine was approved. No comma separates this essential phrase from the main clause. D (no punctuation) is correct.

Text: 'The exhibit featured paintings from three American masters[___] Edward Hopper from New York, Georgia O'Keeffe from New Mexico, and Winslow Homer from Maine.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
A colon introduces a list after a complete independent clause. D (:) is correct. The list that follows explains 'three American masters.'

Text: 'The new algorithm performed exceptionally well on training data[___] it struggled considerably when applied to real-world scenarios.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two contrasting independent clauses. C (semicolon) is the minimal correct fix. B adds 'however' — also correct but adds a word.

Text: 'The research center employs scientists from around the world[___] including Nobel laureates, government advisors, and industry leaders.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Including Nobel laureates, government advisors, and industry leaders' is a non-essential participial phrase. B (,) correctly uses a comma. A semicolon would require an independent clause to follow.

Text: 'The study identified three major risk factors[___] poor diet, sedentary lifestyle, and chronic stress.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

An independent clause ('The study identified three major risk factors') followed by a list. D (:) correctly introduces the list. Both colon and dash would work, but in formal writing a colon is preferred.

Text: 'The scientist[___]who had spent 30 years researching the topic[___]finally announced her breakthrough.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
'Who had spent 30 years researching the topic' is parenthetical information. Em dashes must appear in PAIRS: 'The scientist—who had spent 30 years...—finally announced.' D is correct.

Text: 'Her conclusion was simple[___] the current model was fundamentally flawed.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'Her conclusion was simple' is an independent clause. A colon or dash can introduce the explanation that follows. D (:) is correct (formal). C (—) also works. Both D and C are valid — D is preferred in formal contexts.

Text: 'The award[___]which had never before been given to a non-citizen[___]recognized her lifetime contributions.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
Em dashes must appear in PAIRS around parenthetical information. B (dash and dash) is correct: 'The award—which had never...non-citizen—recognized...'

Text: 'The museum received donations from[___] private collectors, charitable foundations, and government grants.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

A colon CANNOT follow a preposition ('from'). The sentence is complete without any punctuation between 'from' and the list: 'received donations from private collectors, charitable foundations, and government grants.' D (no punctuation) is correct.

Text: 'The new policy accomplished one crucial thing[___]it gave low-income families access to affordable healthcare.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'The new policy accomplished one crucial thing' is a complete independent clause. A colon introduces the explanation. C (:) is correct. D (em dash) would also work. Both are valid; C is the formal choice.

Text: 'Three cities were considered for the summit[___]Geneva, Singapore, and Nairobi.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete independent clause followed by a list. D (:) is correct. C (—) would also work but the colon is more formal.

Text: 'The expedition[___]the first of its kind in over fifty years[___]attracted international media attention.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
Parenthetical information in the middle of a sentence requires em dashes in PAIRS. C (dash and dash) is correct.

Text: 'One conclusion emerged from the data[___]the intervention was only effective for adolescents.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + explanation. C (:) is correct. B (—) also works. C preferred in formal writing.

Text: 'The architect designed three landmark buildings[___]the concert hall, the public library, and the civic center.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause followed by a list of explanatory items. C (:) is correct. B (—) also works.

Text: 'The company's success depended on[___]innovation, strategic partnerships, and market timing.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Colon CANNOT follow a preposition ('on'). D (no punctuation) is correct: 'depended on innovation, strategic partnerships, and market timing.'

Text: 'The finding had one major implication[___]the standard treatment needed to be revised.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + implication explained. C (:) is correct. B (—) also valid. C is formal choice.

Text: 'The committee was divided[___]half supported the proposal, and half opposed it.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The committee was divided' is a complete clause. A colon introduces an explanation. B (:) is correct. A (em dash) would also work.

Text: 'His greatest strength[___]his ability to remain calm under pressure[___]made him an ideal negotiator.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
Parenthetical appositive in the middle of a sentence. Em dashes in PAIRS: 'His greatest strength—his ability to remain calm under pressure—made him...' B is correct.

Text: 'The proposal included only one new provision[___]an annual review of all expenditures.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + specific explanation. B (:) is correct. C (—) also works.

Text: 'The curriculum covered a wide range of topics[___]from ancient history to modern technology.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

'From ancient history to modern technology' is a prepositional phrase modifying 'topics' — not a list introduced after a complete clause. D (no punctuation) is most natural. C (comma) is acceptable but not necessary.

Text: 'The discovery raised a fundamental question[___]how do cells repair themselves without external intervention?'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + a question (the fundamental question). C (:) introduces the specific question. B (em dash) also works for dramatic effect. C is preferred.

Text: 'Three things motivated her[___]ambition, curiosity, and a deep belief in the project's importance.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + list. D (:) is correct. C (—) also works.

Text: 'The results[___]which surprised even the most optimistic researchers[___]showed a 40% improvement.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
Em dashes in PAIRS around parenthetical: 'The results—which surprised even the most optimistic researchers—showed...' A is correct.

Text: 'The policy addressed three systemic issues[___]inadequate funding, unequal resource distribution, and lack of community oversight.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + list. D (:) is correct.

Text: 'The author's central argument[___]that economic inequality drives political instability[___]is supported by data from forty countries.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
Parenthetical appositive in the middle of a sentence: 'The author's central argument—that economic inequality...—is supported.' Em dashes must appear in PAIRS. B is correct.

Text: 'The evidence pointed to one clear conclusion[___]the program had failed to achieve its stated objectives.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete independent clause + explanation. C (:) is correct. D (—) also works but the colon is the formal standard choice here.

Text: 'The renovation transformed the building[___]but the original facade was carefully preserved.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses joined by 'but' (FANBOYS) require a comma before 'but.' C (,) is correct.

Text: 'The panel included experts from[___]behavioral economics, public health, and urban planning.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
A colon CANNOT follow a preposition ('from'). D (no punctuation) is correct: 'from behavioral economics, public health, and urban planning.'

Text: 'Her approach was unlike any other[___]she combined rigorous data analysis with deep ethnographic fieldwork.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + explanation/elaboration. C (:) is correct. B (—) also valid. C is the formal choice.

Text: 'The treaty[___]signed in 1963 by over 100 nations[___]prohibited nuclear testing in the atmosphere.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
Parenthetical information in the middle of a sentence: 'The treaty—signed in 1963 by over 100 nations—prohibited...' Em dashes in PAIRS. B is correct.

Text: 'The challenge was straightforward[___]secure enough funding to complete the final phase of research.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + specific explanation of the challenge. C (:) is correct. D (—) also valid.

Text: 'The documentary examined four cities[___]Lagos, Jakarta, São Paulo, and Mumbai.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + list that explains 'four cities.' C (:) is correct.

Text: 'The data revealed a striking pattern[___]regions with higher education spending consistently showed lower poverty rates.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Complete clause + specific finding that elaborates the pattern. C (:) is correct. D (—) also valid.

Text: 'Her final paper challenged a foundational assumption[___]that language acquisition is primarily genetically determined[___]using evidence from creole languages.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
Parenthetical appositive in the middle. Em dashes in PAIRS: 'challenged a foundational assumption—that language acquisition is primarily genetically determined—using evidence...' B is correct.

Text: 'The company released [___] annual sustainability report last month.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Its' = possessive (belonging to the company). Expand test: 'released it is annual report' → nonsense → use 'its' (no apostrophe). B is correct.

Text: 'The professors [___] lectures on quantum mechanics attracted students from across the university.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Multiple professors → plural → plural possessive: 'professors'' (apostrophe after the s). B is correct. A would mean one professor. C doubles the s — never correct.

Text: 'The researcher presented [___] findings to a panel of international experts.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Hers' is already a possessive pronoun — no apostrophe needed. C is correct. 'Her's' and 'hers'' are not real words.

Text: 'Despite [___] best efforts, the team could not replicate the original experiment's results.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Their' = possessive pronoun (belonging to them). B is correct. A = they are. C = location. D is the expanded form of A.

Text: 'The study examined the [___] responses to the new curriculum across three age groups.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Children' is an irregular plural (does not end in s). Possessive = add 's: 'children's.' A is correct.
