Text: 'The committee reviewed all six [___] proposals before making its final decision.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Multiple candidates (all six) → plural possessive: 'candidates'' (apostrophe after s). B is correct.

Text: 'The [___] new initiative focuses on reducing carbon emissions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
One government → singular possessive: 'government's.' A is correct.

Text: '[___] been over a decade since the discovery was first announced.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'It's been...' = 'It has been...' — a contraction. B (it's) is correct. A (its) is possessive, not a contraction.

Text: 'The scientist [___] research on deep-sea organisms earned her international recognition.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Whose' = possessive relative pronoun (the scientist's research). B is correct. A (who's) = 'who is' — expand test: 'the scientist who is research...' → nonsense.

Text: 'The two [___] offices share the same building but operate completely independently.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two departments → plural → plural possessive: 'departments'' (apostrophe after s). B is correct.

Text: 'The [___] impact on the local ecosystem was studied for three years.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Multiple factories (implied by context) → plural possessive: 'factories'' (apostrophe after s, irregular plural formed with -ies). A is correct.

Text: 'The company announced that [___] expanding operations to three new markets.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'It's expanding' = 'it is expanding' — a contraction. B (it's) is correct.

Text: 'The [___] team won the national championship for the third consecutive year.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Women' is an irregular plural. Add 's for possessive: 'women's.' B is correct. A incorrectly places the apostrophe after 'womens' (not a real word).

Text: 'The [___] argued that the new regulations would stifle innovation.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Regular plural — no apostrophe: 'CEOs.' C is correct. A incorrectly uses apostrophe for a plural. B would mean belonging to the CEOs.

Text: 'The board was impressed by [___] thoroughness and attention to detail.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Her' modifies 'thoroughness' as a possessive adjective. 'Her thoroughness' — 'her' is used here as a determiner (possessive adjective), not the standalone pronoun 'hers.' C (her) is correct.

Text: 'The [___] were asked to evaluate the proposal based on three criteria.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'The reviewers were asked' — no possession indicated. Just a plural subject. C (reviewers, no apostrophe) is correct.

Text: 'The players were pleased with [___] performance in the simulation exercise.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Their performance' = possessive (belonging to the players). B is correct.

Text: 'The [___] evidence suggested a new approach to treatment.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Multiple studies → plural → plural possessive: 'studies'' (apostrophe after s). B is correct. A would mean one study.

Text: 'She doesn't know [___] responsible for the error in the report.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Who's responsible' = 'who is responsible' — a contraction. B (who's) is correct. A (whose) = possessive.

Text: 'The committee published [___] findings in a 200-page report.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Its findings' = possessive (belonging to the committee). B (its) is correct. No apostrophe for possessive pronouns.

Text: 'The [___] attitudes toward remote work have shifted significantly since 2020.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Multiple employees (implied 'attitudes' plural) → plural possessive: 'employees'' (apostrophe after s). B is correct.

Text: 'The conference featured presentations from researchers in the [___].'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Decades do not take apostrophes in the plural: '1990s.' B is correct. A incorrectly uses an apostrophe for the plural.

Text: 'The organization and [___] affiliates released a joint statement.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Its affiliates' — the affiliates belong to the organization (singular) → 'its.' B is correct.

Text: 'The [___] performances exceeded expectations across all three venues.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Multiple orchestras → plural → plural possessive: 'orchestras'' (apostrophe after s). B is correct if referring to multiple orchestras.

Text: 'The scientist explained that the [___] results would be published next month.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
One team → singular possessive: 'team's.' A is correct.

Text: 'The program has achieved [___] primary goal of reducing youth unemployment.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Its primary goal' — possessive (belonging to the program). B (its) is correct. No apostrophe.

Text: 'The [___] research interests span three continents and four decades.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
The context refers to one professor's research interests (singular). A (professor's) is correct.

Text: '[___] been shown that regular exercise reduces the risk of chronic disease.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'It's been shown' = 'It has been shown' — contraction. B is correct.

Text: 'The university changed [___] admission policy to reflect new research on standardized testing.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Its admission policy' — possessive (belonging to the university, singular). B (its) is correct.

Text: 'The [___] findings were later confirmed by an independent research group.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Multiple scientists' findings confirmed → plural possessive: 'scientists'' (apostrophe after s). B is correct.
Which version is a comma splice?
The data was compelling, so the board approved the project immediately.
The data was compelling; the board approved the project immediately.
The data was compelling, the board approved the project immediately.
Because the data was compelling, the board approved the project immediately.
B joins two independent clauses with only a comma — a comma splice.
The weather delayed the launch, and engineers rescheduled for the following week.
The weather delayed the launch engineers rescheduled for the following week.
Although the weather delayed the launch, engineers rescheduled for the following week.
The weather delayed the launch; engineers rescheduled for the following week.
B has two independent clauses with no punctuation or connector — a fused run-on.

Text: 'The novel received mixed reviews upon publication[___] it is now considered a masterpiece of twentieth-century literature.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two contrasting independent clauses. '; however,' correctly shows contrast with semicolon before and comma after.
Which version is a sentence fragment?
The scientist published her findings last month.
The board reviewed all proposals carefully.
B — 'After years of painstaking research' — is a dependent clause with no main clause. Fragment.

Text: 'Solar panels have become significantly cheaper over the past decade[___] many households that previously could not afford them can now install them.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them. A = comma splice. D = run-on.
Which version correctly fixes the fragment 'Discovered in a remote cave in southern France'?
The paintings, discovered in a remote cave in southern France, date back 30,000 years.
Discovered in a remote cave in southern France the paintings date back 30,000 years.
Discovered in a remote cave in southern France, to date back 30,000 years.
Discovered in a remote cave in southern France; the paintings date back 30,000 years.
B attaches the participial phrase to the main sentence: 'The paintings... date back 30,000 years.' Correct sentence structure.

Text: 'The researchers worked around the clock[___] they were determined to publish before the competing team.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) is correct. A = comma splice. D = run-on.
After the team analyzed all available data, it reached a conclusion.
The team analyzed all available data and reached a conclusion.
Having analyzed all available data, the team reached a definitive conclusion.
B is only a participial phrase — no subject, no main verb. Fragment.

Text: 'The population has been declining for years[___] conservationists have been unable to determine the primary cause.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrast: declining but cause unknown. '; yet,' shows contrast with proper semicolon + comma punctuation.
Which version is NOT a fragment?
Although the researchers worked for three years.
The test results were inconclusive, but the study continued.
To determine the cause of the anomaly.
Because the test results were inconclusive.
C has a subject ('the study') and a main verb ('continued'). A, B are dependent clauses alone. D is an infinitive phrase alone.

Text: 'The bridge was structurally sound[___] city engineers ordered it closed after residents reported unusual vibrations.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Sound but still closed — contrast. '; nevertheless,' correctly shows the contrast.
Which version correctly rewrites 'The experiment was a success. Which proved that the hypothesis was correct.' to eliminate the fragment?
The experiment was a success; which proved that the hypothesis was correct.
The experiment was a success, it proved that the hypothesis was correct.
The experiment was a success. That proved that the hypothesis was correct.
The experiment was a success, which proved that the hypothesis was correct.
A attaches 'which proved...' as a nonrestrictive relative clause — no longer a fragment. B incorrectly uses semicolon before a relative clause (not an independent clause). D is a comma splice.

Text: 'The proposal outlined ambitious goals[___] the budget allocated to achieve them was far too limited.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two contrasting independent clauses (ambitious goals but insufficient budget). C (semicolon) correct. B adds 'but' — also valid. A = comma splice.
Exhausted after the long journey, the explorers set up camp immediately.
The long journey exhausted the explorers, who set up camp immediately.
The explorers, exhausted after the long journey, set up camp immediately.
C is only a participial phrase with no subject or main verb — a fragment.

Text: 'Technology has transformed how people consume news[___] younger generations in particular rarely read print newspapers.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correct. A = comma splice. D = run-on.

Text: 'The medication was approved[___] it had only been tested on a small sample population.'

Which logically best completes the text?
Contrast: approved despite limited testing. 'Even though' shows concession/contrast. B is correct.
Which had been conducted over a period of twenty years.
To understand the full implications of the research.
Widely regarded as one of the greatest scientific discoveries of the century.
The discovery, widely regarded as one of the greatest of the century, transformed the field.
D: subject (The discovery) + verb (transformed) — complete sentence. A, B, C are all fragments.

Text: 'The committee met three times[___] it failed to reach a consensus on the key provisions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Three meetings but no consensus — contrast. '; however,' is correct.
Which version correctly fixes the run-on 'The evidence was strong the jury deliberated for only two hours'?
The evidence was strong and the jury deliberated for only two hours.
The evidence, being strong, the jury deliberated for only two hours.
The evidence was strong, the jury deliberated for only two hours.
The evidence was strong; the jury deliberated for only two hours.
A uses a semicolon to correctly join two independent clauses. B is still a comma splice. C omits the necessary comma before 'and.' D is awkward and grammatically unclear.

Text: 'The architect designed a revolutionary building[___] local regulations prevented its construction for a decade.'

Which best completes the text?
Designed but couldn't build — contrast. '; however,' correctly shows this.
To have solved the problem years earlier.
Although they had worked tirelessly toward a solution.
The researchers solved the problem years earlier than expected.
C has subject (researchers) + complete verb (solved). A = infinitive phrase. B = participial phrase. D = dependent clause alone.

Text: 'Ocean temperatures have risen measurably over the past century[___] marine biologists are documenting significant changes in ecosystem behavior.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correct. A = comma splice. D = run-on.
Which version correctly fixes 'Because renewable energy has become cheaper. Many countries are accelerating their transition.'?
Because renewable energy has become cheaper; many countries are accelerating their transition.
Renewable energy has become cheaper. Because many countries are accelerating their transition.
Because renewable energy has become cheaper and many countries are accelerating their transition.
Because renewable energy has become cheaper, many countries are accelerating their transition.
B correctly attaches the dependent clause to the main clause with a comma. A uses semicolon after a dependent clause — wrong. C creates a run-on. D creates a new fragment.

Text: 'The documentary was widely praised by critics[___] audiences found it too slow-paced.'

Which best completes the text?
Praised by critics but disliked by audiences — contrast. B (', yet') uses FANBOYS conjunction correctly. A = comma splice. C (semicolon) also works but B captures the contrast with a conjunction.
The telescope launched in 1990 transformed our understanding of the universe.
The Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, transformed our understanding of the universe.
Launched in 1990, the Hubble Space Telescope transformed our understanding of the universe.
C is only a participial phrase — no subject, no main verb. Fragment.

Text: 'The new treatment showed early promise in clinical trials[___] long-term outcomes remain uncertain.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Promise but uncertainty — contrast. '; however,' correct.
The economy improved slowly, but unemployment remained stubbornly high.
The economy improved slowly unemployment remained stubbornly high.
The economy improved slowly; unemployment remained stubbornly high.
Although the economy improved slowly, unemployment remained stubbornly high.
A: two clauses with no connector and no punctuation — fused run-on.

Text: 'The policy was unpopular with constituents[___] the senator refused to repeal it.'

Which best completes the text?
Unpopular but refused to repeal — contrast. B (', yet') is precise and correct.
Which version is correct (not a fragment or run-on)?
The river flooding the valley destroying crops and displacing families.
When the river flooded the valley destroying crops.
The river flooded the valley it destroyed crops and displaced families.
When the river flooded the valley, it destroyed crops and displaced families.
D: dependent clause + main clause with subject and verb — complete sentence. A is a fragment (no main verb). B is a comma splice. C is a dependent clause fragment.

Text: 'The findings were released to the public[___] they immediately sparked controversy among medical professionals.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. Semicolon correct. A = comma splice.

Text: 'The new stadium seats 80,000 people[___] it has already sold out for every game this season.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses. A = comma splice.
Which fixes the comma splice 'The study was retracted, the methodology was fundamentally flawed'?
The study was retracted, and the methodology was fundamentally flawed.
The study was retracted the methodology was fundamentally flawed.
Both B and C are correct.
The study was retracted; the methodology was fundamentally flawed.
Both B (semicolon) and C (comma + FANBOYS) correctly fix the comma splice. D is correct.

Text: 'The legislation passed with broad support[___] it faced immediate legal challenges from several advocacy groups.'

Which best completes the text?
Passed but challenged — contrast. '; however,' correct.
Which version correctly rewrites the fragment 'Which was eventually awarded a Nobel Prize'?
Which was eventually awarded a Nobel Prize; the research changed medicine.
The research, which was eventually awarded a Nobel Prize, changed medicine.
The research which was eventually awarded a Nobel Prize changed medicine.
The research, which was eventually awarded a Nobel Prize.

B attaches the relative clause as a nonrestrictive element within a complete sentence. A still has no main verb. C uses semicolon before a relative clause. D is missing commas around the nonrestrictive clause.

Text: 'The software update fixed the security vulnerabilities[___] users remained skeptical about the platform's safety.'

Which best completes the text?
Fixed but users still skeptical — contrast/concession. '; nevertheless,' correct.

Text: 'Renewable energy costs have fallen dramatically[___] fossil fuel subsidies continue to distort the market.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Falling costs but distorted market — contrast. '; yet,' correct.

Text: 'The prime minister gave a speech[___] the opposition walked out in protest.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. Semicolon correct. A = comma splice.
Which correctly fixes 'Despite the overwhelming evidence against the theory. Many scientists continued to support it.'?
Despite the overwhelming evidence. Against the theory many scientists continued.
Despite the overwhelming evidence against the theory and many scientists continuing to support it.
Despite the overwhelming evidence against the theory; many scientists continued to support it.
Despite the overwhelming evidence against the theory, many scientists continued to support it.
B attaches the introductory phrase to the main clause with a comma. A uses semicolon after a phrase — wrong.

Text: 'The company launched the product to great fanfare[___] sales never lived up to projections.'

Which best completes the text?
Great launch but poor sales — contrast. '; however,' correct.
After the reactor was shut down, the investigation began.
The reactor was shut down, prompting an immediate investigation.
The reactor was shut down; the investigation immediately began.
The reactor was shut down, the investigation immediately began.
B: two independent clauses joined by comma only — comma splice.

Text: 'The artist spent years in obscurity[___] her work is now displayed in the world's leading galleries.'

Which best completes the text?
Obscurity then fame — contrast/reversal. '; today,' correctly shows this temporal contrast.
Which version is complete (not a fragment)?
The bacteria, which had developed resistance to all known antibiotics.
The bacteria developed resistance to all known antibiotics.
Developing resistance to all known antibiotics.
To develop resistance to all known antibiotics.
C: subject + verb — complete. A = relative clause with no main verb. B = participial phrase. D = infinitive phrase.

Text: 'The infrastructure was aging[___] the government had delayed necessary repairs for budget reasons.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. Semicolon correct. A = comma splice.
Which correctly fixes the run-on 'The ocean contains vast untapped resources their extraction raises serious environmental concerns'?
The ocean contains vast untapped resources, their extraction raises serious environmental concerns.
The ocean contains vast untapped resources; their extraction raises serious environmental concerns.
The ocean contains vast untapped resources; however, their extraction raises serious environmental concerns.
Both B and C are correct.
Both B (with contrast signal) and C (semicolon alone) correctly fix the run-on. D is correct.

Text: 'The athlete trained for a decade[___] a career-ending injury struck six months before the Olympic trials.'

Which best completes the text?
Ten years of work then sudden injury — tragic contrast. '; tragically,' precisely captures the tone.
The glacier has retreated significantly since measurements began in 1980.
Retreating at an unprecedented rate due to rising global temperatures.
Scientists have recorded unprecedented rates of glacial retreat.
The glacier's retreat has accelerated measurably over the past decade.
B: participial phrase with no subject or main verb — fragment.

Text: 'The new regulations reduced emissions[___] they also increased production costs for small manufacturers.'

Which correctly completes the text?
Two independent clauses. Semicolon correct. A = comma splice.
When the satellite malfunctioned, engineers scrambled to reestablish contact.
The satellite malfunctioned, engineers scrambled to reestablish contact.
The satellite malfunctioned; engineers scrambled to reestablish contact.
The satellite malfunctioned, forcing engineers to scramble to reestablish contact.
B: comma splice (two independent clauses, comma only).

Text: 'The excavation revealed thousands of artifacts[___] most were too fragile to transport without specialized equipment.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Semicolon correctly joins the two clauses. A = comma splice. B adds 'however' — also valid but C is cleaner.
Which correctly identifies and fixes the error in: 'The museum was renovated it now attracts three times as many visitors.'?
The museum that was renovated now attracting three times as many visitors.
The museum was renovated, three times as many visitors now come.
The museum was renovated; it now attracts three times as many visitors.
The museum was renovated, it now attracts three times as many visitors.
The original is a run-on. A correctly uses a semicolon to join the two independent clauses. B is a comma splice. C changes meaning. D is a fragment.

Text: 'The preliminary findings were encouraging[___] the lead scientist cautioned against drawing firm conclusions.'

Which best completes the text?
Encouraging but cautioned — contrast/concession. '; nevertheless,' correct.

Text: 'Urban farming has expanded rapidly[___] it faces significant challenges related to land cost and water access.'

Which best completes the text?
Expanded but faces challenges — contrast. '; however,' is the conjunctive adverb form. B ('; but') — semicolons should not precede FANBOYS. C is correct.
Which fixes the fragment 'Although widely considered the greatest novelist of her generation'?
Although widely considered the greatest novelist of her generation; she published only four books.
Although widely considered the greatest novelist of her generation. She published only four books.
Although widely considered the greatest novelist of her generation, she published only four books.
She published only four books although widely considered the greatest novelist of her generation.
A and D both create complete sentences. A uses the fragment as an introductory clause. D reverses the order. Both are correct, but A is listed first. A is the answer.

Text: 'The theory was elegant[___] it failed to account for several key experimental observations.'

Which best completes the text?
Elegant but flawed — contrast. '; however,' correct.
Which version correctly fixes the dangling modifier?
The samples, returning from the field, were carefully labeled.
Returning from the field, the samples were carefully labeled by the team.
The team's samples returning from the field were carefully labeled.
Returning from the field, the team carefully labeled the samples.
'Returning from the field' — who returned? The team. Subject after comma must be 'the team.' B is correct.
The CEO was praised for her vision, her work ethic, and her willingness to take bold risks.
The CEO was praised for having vision, her work ethic, and taking bold risks.
The CEO was praised for her vision, her work ethic, and taking bold risks.
The CEO was praised for vision, her work ethic, and that she took bold risks.
B: three parallel noun phrases — 'her vision, her work ethic, her willingness.' All possessive noun phrases. A mixes nouns and a gerund. C and D mix forms.
Which version corrects the dangling modifier 'Having examined the patient, the diagnosis was made'?
Having examined the patient, the diagnosis was made.
The patient, having been examined, the diagnosis was made.
A diagnosis was made, having examined the patient.
Having examined the patient, the doctor made a diagnosis.
'Having examined the patient' — the doctor examined. B: subject after comma = 'the doctor.' Correct.
Which version is NOT correctly parallel?
She enjoys reading novels, watching films, and hiking trails.
He is talented, dedicated, and works very hard.
The course covers theory, practice, and application.
The study was comprehensive, rigorous, and well-documented.
B mixes adjectives (talented, dedicated) with a verb phrase (works very hard). Should be: 'talented, dedicated, and hardworking.'
Which placement of 'nearly' gives the meaning that almost all homes were affected?
The storm destroyed every home nearly in the neighborhood.
Nearly the storm destroyed every home in the neighborhood.
The storm nearly destroyed every home in the neighborhood.
The storm destroyed nearly every home in the neighborhood.
B: 'nearly every home' — 'nearly' directly modifies 'every home.' A: 'nearly destroyed' means the storm came close to destroying. B is correct for the intended meaning.
Which version uses 'not only...but also' correctly?
The vaccine not only preventing the disease but also reduces its severity.
The vaccine not only prevents the disease but also it reduces severity.
The vaccine not only prevents the disease but also reducing its severity.
The vaccine not only prevents the disease but also reduces its severity.
B: 'not only PREVENTS...but also REDUCES' — both base verbs, parallel. A ends with a gerund. C begins with a gerund. D adds 'it' unnecessarily.
Which version corrects the misplaced modifier?
On paper plates, she served cake to the children.
She served to the children cake on paper plates.
She served cake on paper plates to the children.
She served cake to the children on paper plates.
'On paper plates' should modify 'cake' (the cake was on paper plates, not the children). C: 'cake on paper plates to the children' — modifier is adjacent to 'cake.' Correct.
Which version corrects the dangling modifier 'Written during the Great Depression, readers found the novel deeply moving'?
Readers found the novel, written during the Great Depression, deeply moving.
Written during the Great Depression, readers found the novel deeply moving.
Written during the Great Depression, the novel was found deeply moving by readers.
The novel, written during the Great Depression, readers found deeply moving.
'Written during the Great Depression' modifies 'the novel.' C places the modifier immediately after 'the novel' as a nonrestrictive element — correct. B also works. C is cleaner.
Which version makes a correct parallel comparison?
Both B and C are correct.
The population of Tokyo is larger than New York's.
The population of Tokyo is larger than New York.
The population of Tokyo is larger than the population of New York.
B (Tokyo's population vs. New York's) and C (Tokyo's population vs. New York's population) both correctly compare population to population. D is correct.
Which correctly fixes the dangling modifier 'To pass the course, regular attendance is required'?
Both B and C are correct.
To pass the course, students must attend regularly.
To pass the course, regular attendance is required.
Regular attendance is required to pass the course.
A is a dangling modifier (attendance doesn't pass courses; students do). B fixes the subject. C restructures. Both B and C are correct. D is the answer.
'The scientist observed the samples using a high-powered microscope.' The modifier 'using a high-powered microscope' is ambiguous. Which revision is clearest?
Using a high-powered microscope, the scientist observed the samples.
Using a high-powered microscope, the samples were observed by the scientist.
The scientist, using a high-powered microscope, observed the samples.
Both B and C are correct.
B and C both correctly attach 'using a high-powered microscope' to 'the scientist' (the person using the microscope). Both are clear and grammatically correct. D is the answer.
The policy is both controversial and wide criticism has followed.
The policy is both controversial and widely criticized.
The policy is both controversial and it has been widely criticized.
The policy both is controversial and widely criticized.
B: 'both CONTROVERSIAL and WIDELY CRITICIZED' — both adjective phrases parallel. A mixes adjective and clause. C is awkward. D mixes adjective and clause.

Which version correctly places the limiting modifier 'just'?

Intended meaning: She told him (and no one else).
She just told him the news.
She told him just the news.
Just she told him the news.
She told just him the news.
B: 'told JUST HIM' — 'just' immediately precedes 'him,' limiting who was told. A: 'just told' modifies the action. C: 'just the news' limits what was told. D is ungrammatical.
Which version corrects the error in 'The professor graded the papers in her office that the students had submitted'?
Both B and C are correct.
The professor graded the papers that the students had submitted in her office.
In her office, the professor graded the papers the students had submitted.
The professor, in her office, graded the papers that the students had submitted.
The original implies the students submitted papers in her office. B and C both correctly place the action 'in her office' as something the professor did. Both are correct — D is the answer.
He was praised for his intelligence, creativity, and work ethic.
The study examined poverty, inequality, and social mobility.
The company focuses on innovation, sustainability, and growth.
She values honesty, loyalty, and acts with integrity.
B mixes nouns (honesty, loyalty) with a verb phrase (acts with integrity). Should be: 'honesty, loyalty, and integrity.'
Which version makes the comparison correctly?
Both B and C are correct.
The winters in Canada are harsher than those in Mexico.
The winters in Canada are harsher than Mexico's winters are.
The winters in Canada are harsher than Mexico.
B (Canada's winters vs. 'those' in Mexico = those winters) and C (Canada's winters vs. Mexico's winters) both compare winters to winters. D is correct.
Which version corrects the dangling modifier 'As a seasoned traveler, packing light has become second nature'?
Packing light, as a seasoned traveler, has become second nature.
As a seasoned traveler, she has found that packing light becomes second nature.
As a seasoned traveler, packing light has become second nature.
For a seasoned traveler, packing light has become second nature.

A: 'packing light' doesn't travel — dangling. B fixes the subject (she). D restructures with 'for,' making it a prepositional phrase rather than a dangling modifier — also correct. D is the cleanest fix.
Which is correctly parallel with 'not only...but also'?
The renovation not only improved aesthetics but also it was more energy-efficient.
The renovation not only improved aesthetics but also increased energy efficiency.
The renovation not only improved aesthetics but also being more energy-efficient.
The renovation not only improved aesthetics but also the building became more energy-efficient.
B: 'not only IMPROVED...but also INCREASED' — both past tense verbs. Parallel.
Which version contains a misplaced modifier?
The researcher conducted the experiment in the laboratory carefully.
The professor graded papers at her desk that students had submitted online.
The astronaut nearly completed every experiment on the mission.
The children watched the fireworks from the rooftop with delight.
D: 'that students had submitted online' should modify 'papers,' but its position makes it seem to modify 'desk.' Revised: 'The professor graded papers that students had submitted online.'
The author is known for her vivid imagery, complex characters, and how she plots her stories.
The author is known for creating vivid imagery, having complex characters, and plots that are intricate.
The author is known for imagery that is vivid, characters who are complex, and how she plots.
The author is known for her vivid imagery, complex characters, and intricate plots.
B: three parallel noun phrases — 'vivid imagery, complex characters, intricate plots.' A, C, D mix forms.
Which version correctly fixes the dangling modifier 'Exhausted from the long journey, the hotel room was a welcome sight'?
A welcome sight was the hotel room exhausted from the long journey.
The hotel room, exhausted from the long journey, was a welcome sight.
Exhausted from the long journey, the travelers found the hotel room a welcome sight.
Exhausted from the long journey, the hotel room was a welcome sight.
'Exhausted from the long journey' — the travelers were exhausted (not the hotel room). C: subject = 'the travelers.' Correct.
Which correctly compares like with like?
Both B and C are correct.
The results of the study were more significant than the earlier research produced.
The results of the study were more significant than those of the earlier research.
The results of the study were more significant than the earlier research.
B (results vs. 'those' = results of earlier research) and C (results vs. what earlier research produced) both make valid comparisons. D is correct.
Which correctly fixes the dangling modifier 'To become a licensed pilot, hundreds of hours of flight training are required'?
Both B and C are correct.
To become a licensed pilot, hundreds of hours of flight training are required.
Hundreds of hours of flight training are required to become a licensed pilot.
To become a licensed pilot, one must complete hundreds of hours of flight training.
A: 'flight training' doesn't become a pilot — dangling. B fixes with 'one' as subject. C restructures as a non-dangling infinitive. Both correct. D is the answer.
Which version correctly fixes the dangling modifier 'Working overtime for months, the project was finally completed'?
The project, working overtime for months, was finally completed.
Working overtime for months, the team finally completed the project.
Working overtime for months, the project was finally completed.
Finally completed, the team worked overtime for months on the project.
'Working overtime' — who worked? The team. C: subject = 'the team.' Correct.
Which version contains a dangling modifier?
Having trained for years, the athlete was ready for the competition.
Trained by experienced coaches, the athlete performed brilliantly.
The athlete, having trained for years, was ready for the competition.
Having trained for years, the competition began.
C: 'Having trained for years' — the competition didn't train. Dangling modifier.
Which correctly places 'even' to mean 'she won every match, including the hardest one'?
She won even every match in the tournament.
She won every even match in the tournament.
Even she won every match in the tournament.
She won every match, even the most difficult one.
B: 'even the most difficult one' — 'even' emphasizes the surprising inclusion of the hardest match. A is ungrammatical. C implies surprise that she (and not someone else) won. D changes meaning.
The board either will approve or will reject the proposal.
The board will either approve the proposal or it will be rejected.
Either the board will approve the proposal or rejection will occur.
The board will either approve or reject the proposal.
B: 'either APPROVE or REJECT' — both bare verbs. Parallel. A: approve (verb) vs. it will be rejected (clause). C and D are awkward.
Which version correctly fixes the dangling modifier 'After reviewing all applications, the position was awarded to Dr. Kim'?
After reviewing all applications, the committee awarded the position to Dr. Kim.
Dr. Kim was awarded the position after reviewing all applications.
The position, after reviewing all applications, was awarded to Dr. Kim.
After reviewing all applications, the position was awarded to Dr. Kim.
'After reviewing all applications' — the committee reviewed. B: subject = 'the committee.' Correct.
Which placement of 'only' conveys 'the committee approved exactly one proposal'?
The committee only approved one proposal.
Only the committee approved one proposal.
The committee approved one only proposal.
The committee approved only one proposal.
B: 'approved ONLY ONE proposal' — 'only' limits 'one proposal' (the quantity). A: 'only approved' could mean the committee merely approved it (didn't discuss, etc.). B is correct.
Which version correctly fixes 'Being a difficult subject, many students struggle with calculus'?
Both B and C are correct.
Being a difficult subject, many students struggle with calculus.
Being a difficult subject, calculus challenges many students.
Because calculus is a difficult subject, many students struggle with it.

A: students aren't 'being a difficult subject' — dangling. B restructures with a subordinate clause. C: 'Being a difficult subject' modifies 'calculus' (calculus is the difficult subject, and it's now the subject). Both correct. D is the answer.
Which correctly fixes 'To improve public health, more funding needs to be allocated to preventive care'?
Both A and B could be correct depending on context.
To improve public health, more funding needs to be allocated to preventive care.
To improve public health, policymakers need to allocate more funding to preventive care.
More funding needs to be allocated to improve public health in preventive care.
A: 'more funding' doesn't improve public health — dangling. B: subject = 'policymakers' who actually do the improving. C restructures but slightly changes meaning. B is the cleanest fix.
Neither the mayor nor the council members were available for comment.
Neither the mayor was available nor the council members were for comment.
Neither the mayor nor the council members was available for comment.
Neither were the mayor nor the council members available for comment.
'Neither X nor Y': verb agrees with closest subject (council members = plural → were). B is correct.
Which correctly fixes the dangling modifier 'Determined to finish the marathon, the finish line finally came into view'?
Determined to finish the marathon, the finish line finally came into view.
The finish line, determined to finish the marathon, finally came into view.
Finally seeing the finish line, she was determined to finish the marathon.
Determined to finish the marathon, she finally saw the finish line.
'Determined to finish' — the runner was determined (not the finish line). B: subject = 'she.' Correct.
She is known for her research, her teaching, and her mentorship.
The study sought to measure outcomes, identify trends, and to make recommendations.
The company focuses on innovation, quality, and customer satisfaction.
The policy aims to reduce inequality, strengthen communities, and expand opportunity.

B mixes 'to measure, identify' with 'to make' — technically this is parallel (all have 'to'), but the last 'to make' breaks the rhythm of shared 'to.' More importantly: 'sought to measure, identify, and to make' — the 'to' is repeated inconsistently. A, C, D are consistently parallel.
Which version correctly places the modifier?
The scientist discovered a new compound with her team that could treat cancer.
With her team, the scientist discovered a new compound that could treat cancer.
The scientist with her team discovered a new compound that could treat cancer.
Both B and C are correct.
Both B and C correctly place the team context and the relative clause 'that could treat cancer' directly after 'compound.' D is correct.
Which correctly fixes 'After completing the experiment, the results were analyzed'?
The results were analyzed after completing the experiment.
After completing the experiment, the results were analyzed.
After completing the experiment, the team analyzed the results.
The results, after completing the experiment, were analyzed.
'After completing' — who completed? The team. B: subject = 'the team.' Correct.

Text: 'In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that mold [___] the bacteria in his petri dish, leading to the discovery of penicillin.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
The passage describes events in 1928 (past). 'Was killing' = past progressive, showing the ongoing action at the time of his observation. D is correct.

Text: 'By the time the rescue team reached the stranded climbers, temperatures [___] below freezing for over eighteen hours.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'By the time [past event]' requires PAST PERFECT to show the temperature drop preceded the rescue. B (had dropped) is correct.

Text: 'The committee recommended that the new facilities [___] accessible to all students with disabilities.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Recommended that' + SUBJECT + BASE VERB (subjunctive). C (be) is correct.

Text: 'If the treatment [___] more affordable, many patients who currently cannot access it would benefit significantly.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact condition (treatment is NOT currently affordable). 'Were' for all subjects in hypothetical conditions. C is correct.

Text: 'Researchers studying the fossilized remains [___] that the species went extinct approximately 65 million years ago.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Present perfect (have concluded) shows ongoing/current relevance — researchers have concluded (and this is the current scientific understanding). A is correct.

Text: 'If the proposal [___] submitted before the deadline, it would have been considered for funding.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past (it was NOT submitted): 'If it HAD BEEN submitted' + 'would have been considered.' C (had been) is correct.

Text: 'The policy required that every employee [___] a mandatory safety training course before beginning work.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Required that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (complete) is correct.

Text: 'By 2030, the company [___] all of its operations to renewable energy sources.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'By 2030' (a future deadline) + FUTURE PERFECT to show completion by that point. C (will have converted) is correct.

Text: 'When the archaeologists [___] the site, they found evidence of a civilization far older than previously thought.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Sequential past events: 'excavated...found.' Both in simple past since they happened at roughly the same time (the finding was part of the excavation). D is correct.

Text: 'The judge insisted that the witness [___] the entire transcript without interruption.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Insisted that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. B (read) is correct.

Text: 'Scientists [___] that the average global temperature has risen by approximately 1.1°C since pre-industrial times.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Current scientific consensus with past-to-present relevance → PRESENT PERFECT. C (have estimated) is correct.

Text: 'If renewable energy [___] cheaper faster, the transition from fossil fuels would have occurred decades earlier.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past: 'If it HAD BECOME cheaper' + 'would have occurred.' B is correct.

Text: 'Before the invention of the printing press, monks [___] manuscripts by hand for centuries.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Before [past event]' — copying preceded the invention → PAST PERFECT. C (had copied) is correct.

Text: 'The council proposed that a new park [___] in the center of the city.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Proposed that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive = be + past participle). C (be built) is correct.

Text: 'If the engineer [___] the calculations correctly, the structure would not have collapsed.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past: 'If the engineer HAD checked' + 'would not have collapsed.' B is correct.

Text: 'Darwin observed that species [___] over time through a process of natural selection.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Darwin's observation describes a GENERAL TRUTH (species do change). Even in a historical context, general truths use PRESENT TENSE. C (change) is correct.

Text: 'The survey [___] that public confidence in institutions has declined significantly over the past two decades.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
A specific past survey finding → SIMPLE PAST. B (found) is correct.

Text: 'The regulations demanded that all products [___] for safety before being sold to consumers.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Demanded that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive = be + past participle). C (be tested) is correct.

Text: 'By the time the election results were announced, supporters [___] for hours outside the counting center.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'By the time [past event]' + ongoing prior action → PAST PERFECT PROGRESSIVE. C (had been waiting) is correct.

Text: 'If the negotiations [___] successful, the trade agreement would have been signed last year.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past: 'If negotiations HAD BEEN successful' + 'would have been signed.' B is correct.

Text: 'The professor urged that each student [___] the primary sources rather than relying on secondary analyses.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Urged that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. B (read) is correct.

Text: 'Since the introduction of the new system, errors [___] by more than 40%.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Since [past event]' + ongoing effect to present → PRESENT PERFECT. C (have been reduced) is correct.

Text: 'If the weather [___] better tomorrow, the outdoor exhibition will proceed as planned.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
REAL/POSSIBLE condition (weather might be better): 'If + present → will.' B (is) is correct.

Text: 'The scientist suggested that the committee [___] the data before drawing conclusions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Suggested that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (review) is correct.

Text: 'Historians now know that the Roman Empire [___] its peak influence around 117 CE under Emperor Trajan.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Specific historical event at a specific time → SIMPLE PAST. A (reached) is correct.

Text: 'The architects proposed that the building [___] LEED platinum certification standards.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Proposed that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (meet) is correct.

Text: 'By the time future historians examine these records, the era [___] the most transformative in human history.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Future deadline ('by the time future historians examine') → FUTURE PERFECT. C (will have been) is correct.

Text: 'If the company [___] its marketing strategy earlier, it might have avoided the dramatic loss in market share.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past: 'If it HAD changed' + 'might have avoided.' C is correct.

Text: 'The director required that every scene [___] three times before being approved for the final cut.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Required that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive). C (be shot) is correct.

Text: 'Before the pharmaceutical trial ended, researchers [___] a promising reduction in symptoms across all age groups.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Before [past event]' — observation preceded the end of trial → PAST PERFECT. C (had observed) is correct.

Text: 'If water [___] at a lower temperature, ice skating on natural ponds would be possible in more climates.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact: water doesn't freeze at a lower temperature. 'Were' or past tense. B (froze) is correct for hypothetical.

Text: 'The international treaty required that each signatory nation [___] its greenhouse gas emissions by 30% within a decade.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Required that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (reduce) is correct.

Text: 'Newton developed his laws of motion, which [___] the foundation for classical mechanics for over two centuries.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Historical past — Newton's laws provided that foundation in the past. B (provided) is correct in historical context.

Text: 'Had the researchers published their findings earlier, the medical community [___] had more time to evaluate the treatment.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past: 'Had they published' (= 'If they had published') + 'would have had.' B is correct.

Text: 'The board demanded that the CEO [___] a full explanation for the financial discrepancies at the next meeting.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Demanded that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (provide) is correct.

Text: 'The geologists discovered that the rock formations [___] over millions of years through gradual volcanic activity.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Formation happened before the discovery → PAST PERFECT. C (had formed) is correct.

Text: 'If the city invests in public transportation now, commute times [___] significantly within five years.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
REAL condition (the city could invest): 'If + present → will.' A (will decrease) is correct.

Text: 'The professor insisted that the papers [___] submitted in the format specified in the syllabus.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Insisted that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive = be + past participle). C (be) is correct.

Text: 'Since the dam [___] in 1936, it has provided water to millions of residents in the surrounding region.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Specific past event (1936) + present perfect in second clause. The dam was built in 1936 (simple past). B is correct.

Text: 'If the defendant [___] not guilty, the prosecution would appeal the verdict.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Hypothetical/contrary-to-fact: 'were found' — the conditional expressing a hypothetical verdict. B is correct.

Text: 'The ancient Egyptians believed that the sun god Ra [___] across the sky each day in a solar barge.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Historical belief in the past → SIMPLE PAST. B (traveled) is correct.

Text: 'By the time the documentary is released, the production team [___] over four years on the project.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Future deadline ('by the time [future event]') → FUTURE PERFECT. C (will have spent) is correct.

Text: 'The researcher proposed that the sample size [___] tripled to ensure statistical significance.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Proposed that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive). C (be) is correct.

Text: 'If the union [___] the contract, the strike would have been avoided entirely.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past (the union did NOT accept): 'If it HAD ACCEPTED' + 'would have been avoided.' C is correct.

Text: 'The court ruling established that corporations [___] certain constitutional protections.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Current legal truth/general principle → PRESENT TENSE even within a past-tense context. A (have) is correct.

Text: 'Ever since the introduction of the new policy, employee satisfaction scores [___] consistently.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Ever since [past event]' + ongoing to present → PRESENT PERFECT. D (have risen) is correct.

Text: 'If I [___] the report more carefully, I would have caught the error before it was submitted.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past: 'If I HAD reviewed' + 'would have caught.' C is correct.

Text: 'The commission recommended that the city [___] funding for public housing by 20% over the next five years.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Recommended that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (increase) is correct.

Text: 'When the first explorers arrived, indigenous communities [___] in the region for thousands of years.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'When [past arrival]' — living preceded arrival → PAST PERFECT PROGRESSIVE showing extended action before another past event. C (had been living) is correct.

Text: 'If the infrastructure were modernized, businesses [___] more likely to invest in the region.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Hypothetical condition ('if...were') → hypothetical result 'would be.' D is correct.

Text: 'The historian argued that the revolution [___] inevitable given the social and economic conditions of the time.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Reported historical judgment in past tense → SIMPLE PAST. B (was) is correct.

Text: 'The ethics committee required that all human subjects research [___] approved by an institutional review board.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Required that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive). C (be) is correct.

Text: 'The company [___] steadily for three decades before the market downturn reversed its fortunes.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Growth preceded the downturn → PAST PERFECT. C (had grown) is correct.

Text: 'If the scientists publish their results, other researchers [___] able to reproduce the experiment.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
REAL condition (they might publish): 'If + present → will.' B (will be) is correct.

Text: 'As if he [___] the expert, the undergraduate student confidently corrected the professor's calculation.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'As if' introduces a CONTRARY-TO-FACT comparison (he is not the expert) → 'were.' C is correct.

Text: 'The senator insisted that the bill [___] tabled until more evidence was gathered.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Insisted that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive). C (be) is correct.

Text: 'By the time they reached the summit, the climbers [___] for sixteen hours without rest.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'By the time [past event]' + extended prior action → PAST PERFECT PROGRESSIVE. C (had been climbing) is correct.

Text: 'If the development had been planned more thoughtfully, the wetlands [___] preserved.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past: 'If...had been planned' → 'would have been preserved.' C is correct.

Text: 'Newton's third law states that every action [___] an equal and opposite reaction.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Scientific law = PERMANENT TRUTH → present tense regardless of context. B (has) is correct.

Text: 'The governor proposed that a bipartisan commission [___] established to review the findings.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Proposed that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive). C (be) is correct.

The expedition carried only what was essential ______ rope, rations, a compass, and a battered map.

Which choice conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

A colon introduces the list after a complete independent clause ('The expedition carried only what was essential'). A semicolon needs two independent clauses; the comma and no-punctuation options create errors.

Which choice conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

______, the ancient manuscript revealed details no historian had anticipated.
Having restored it over many years

The modifier must logically describe the manuscript that follows. 'Painstakingly restored over many years' correctly modifies 'the ancient manuscript.' The others dangle or imply the manuscript did the restoring.
Mixed Review:
Text: 'The grant supports researchers studying the effects of deep-sea mining on benthic ecosystems, the sediment communities that [___] the ocean floor.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'That' refers to 'communities' (plural). Plural → 'populate.' A is correct.

Text: 'Although the original hypothesis was not supported by the data, the researchers [___] their methodology to be sound.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Historical research conclusion → simple past. B (found) is correct.

Passage: 'Photovoltaic cells convert sunlight into electricity. This process is clean and renewable. However, the manufacturing of solar panels requires significant energy and rare earth materials.'

Which transition best introduces a sentence about long-term sustainability assessments?
Adding more information about sustainability → 'furthermore.' D is correct.
Claim: 'The introduction of wolves to Yellowstone restored the park's ecological balance.' Which evidence best supports this?
Wolves were hunted to extinction in Yellowstone by the 1920s.
Many visitors to Yellowstone hope to observe wolves in the wild.
Wolves are apex predators found across the Northern Hemisphere.
After wolf reintroduction in 1995, vegetation recovered in areas previously overgrazed by elk, whose behavior changed in response to wolf predation.
B directly supports the mechanism: wolf reintroduction → changed elk behavior → vegetation recovery → ecological balance. A is background. C is general. D is tourist preference.

Text: 'The committee's report neither acknowledged the limitations of the study [___] proposed concrete solutions to the problems it identified.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither X nor Y' — B (nor) completes the correlative conjunction correctly.

Passage: 'Maria Sibylla Merian was a seventeenth-century naturalist and artist who traveled to Suriname to study tropical insects. Her detailed scientific illustrations challenged prevailing misconceptions about insect metamorphosis. As used in the text, 'prevailing' most nearly means:
'Prevailing misconceptions' = the misconceptions that were dominant/widely accepted at the time. B is correct.

Text: 'The city's infrastructure [___] to deteriorate rapidly without significant investment, according to a new engineering assessment.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
The policy which was enacted in 2019, has been widely criticized.
The policy, which was enacted in 2019 has been widely criticized.
The policy, which was enacted in 2019, has been widely criticized.
The policy which was enacted in 2019 has been widely criticized.
'Which was enacted in 2019' is NONRESTRICTIVE — extra info about a specific policy. Commas on BOTH sides. C is correct.

Text: 'If the new treatment [___] effective in the current trials, the FDA would fast-track its approval.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Hypothetical condition (not yet proven) → 'were to prove' uses subjunctive-style hypothetical. C is correct.

Passage: 'Recent data suggests that the rate of species extinction has accelerated dramatically. Scientists now estimate that species are disappearing up to 1,000 times faster than the natural background rate.' Which choice best states the main idea?
Contemporary species loss is occurring at a rate dramatically higher than the natural background rate.
B captures both elements: the acceleration AND the comparison to natural background rate. A is too vague. C is too general. D misses the 'dramatically accelerated' element. B is correct.
The womens' team won their third consecutive championship.
The women's team won their third consecutive championship.
The womens team won its third consecutive championship.
The women's team won its third consecutive championship.
'Women' is an irregular plural → add 's for possessive: 'women's.' 'Team' is singular → 'its.' B is correct.

Text: 'Having mapped the genome, [___] began the painstaking work of identifying the functions of individual genes.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Having mapped the genome' — who mapped? The researchers. C correctly makes 'the researchers' the subject after the participial phrase.

Passage: 'The architect believed that form should follow function. Every element of her design served a practical purpose; no decorative flourishes existed merely for aesthetic appeal.' As used in the text, 'flourishes' most nearly means:
'Decorative flourishes' = ornamental additions for appearance. B (embellishments) is correct.

Text: 'Neither of the two medications [___] been shown to be consistently effective in clinical trials.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither' as a subject = SINGULAR → has. B is correct.
The study raised: three concerns, the sample was small, the follow-up period was brief.
The study raised three concerns: the sample was small, the follow-up period was brief, and the methodology was inconsistently applied.
The study raised three concerns, the sample was small, the follow-up period was brief, and the methodology was inconsistently applied.
The study raised three concerns; the sample was small, the follow-up period was brief, and the methodology was inconsistently applied.
Independent clause + colon introduces a list. A is correct. B uses semicolon (needs two independent clauses). C is a comma splice. D places the colon after 'raised' (after a verb — wrong).

Text: 'By 2030, nearly half of all new car sales worldwide [___] electric vehicles, according to current projections.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Future projection ('by 2030') → future tense. C (will be) is correct.
Which version is NOT a sentence fragment?
Despite the unprecedented scale and the widespread damage it caused.
Because of the unprecedented scale of the environmental disaster.
Causing widespread damage to coastal ecosystems and fishing communities.
The environmental disaster caused unprecedented damage to coastal ecosystems.
C: subject (disaster) + verb (caused) — complete sentence. A, B, D are all fragments.

Text: 'The policy [___] significant opposition from industry groups, who argued it would increase operating costs by up to 30%.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Context is past (the policy received opposition) → simple past. B (faced) is correct.

Passage: 'The development of CRISPR technology represents a potential revolution in medicine. Researchers have already used it to treat sickle cell disease, and clinical trials for dozens of other genetic conditions are underway. However, the technology's use in germline editing — modifying embryos in ways that would be inherited by future generations — remains deeply controversial.' Which transition would best introduce a sentence about international governance?
Furthermore, CRISPR has many other applications.
This controversy has prompted calls for international governance frameworks to ensure responsible development.

C isn't just a transition signal — it IS the sentence, providing the natural next step: controversy → calls for governance. The stem asks for a transition; C serves as the transitional sentence. C is correct.

Text: 'The bridge [___] under construction for seven years before it was finally opened to traffic in 1937.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Before it was...opened' — construction preceded opening → PAST PERFECT. C (had been) is correct.
Which version correctly fixes 'The board discussed the proposal, it was rejected unanimously'?
The board discussed the proposal; and it was rejected unanimously.
The board discussed the proposal; it was rejected unanimously.
The board discussed the proposal it was rejected unanimously.
The board discussed the proposal, however it was rejected unanimously.
B uses a semicolon to correctly join two independent clauses. A is a run-on. C uses semicolon + FANBOYS (wrong). D uses a comma before 'however' (comma splice).

Text: 'The evidence strongly [___] that childhood nutrition programs improve long-term academic outcomes.'

Context: Multiple longitudinal studies with large sample sizes.

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Multiple longitudinal studies + large samples = strong evidence → 'indicates.' D is correct. B and C are too hedged for this level of evidence.
The report recommended that new staff would be hired, training existing employees, and a budget increase.
The report recommended hiring new staff, to train existing employees, and a budget increase.
The report recommended to hire new staff, train existing employees, and budget increases.
The report recommended hiring new staff, training existing employees, and increasing the budget.
B: three parallel gerunds — 'hiring, training, increasing.' A, C, D mix forms.

Text: 'If the satellite data [___] earlier, the team could have predicted the hurricane's path with greater accuracy.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Contrary-to-fact past: 'If it HAD BEEN analyzed' + 'could have predicted.' A is correct.

Passage: 'The study examined three approaches to reducing food waste: source reduction, food redistribution, and recycling. The first approach — preventing excess food from being produced — proved most effective in terms of both environmental impact and cost savings.' Which choice best states the main idea?
Source reduction is more effective than redistribution or recycling for addressing food waste.
Food waste is a serious problem.
Food waste has environmental and economic consequences.
Three approaches to food waste were studied.
B captures the comparative finding: source reduction > other approaches, on two criteria. A is too general. C is background. D describes the study's structure but not its finding. B is correct.
The recipe requires only three ingredients: flour, eggs, and butter.
You need: flour, eggs, and butter.
The recipe: requires flour, eggs, and butter.
The ingredients are: flour, eggs, and butter.

B: 'The recipe requires only three ingredients' is a complete independent clause before the colon. A and C place the colon after 'are' and 'need' (verbs — wrong). D places it after 'the recipe' (incomplete). B is correct.

Text: 'The committee, having reviewed all submissions, [___] that the first-place entry was significantly stronger than the others.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Having reviewed' is a past participial phrase. Past context → simple past main verb. B (concluded) is correct.
The company announced they would reduce its workforce by 15%.
The company announced that they would reduce their workforce by 15%.
The company announced it would reduce their workforce by 15%.
The company announced that it would reduce its workforce by 15%.
'The company' = singular → 'it' and 'its.' B is correct.

Text: 'Researchers in the field [___] that the new approach could reduce treatment times by half, though larger trials are needed to confirm this.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Larger trials are needed to confirm' = preliminary, unconfirmed → hedging language. B (speculate) is appropriate. A and C overclaim. D is wordy and informal.

Text: 'The discovery — which had eluded scientists for decades — [___] the prevailing model of protein folding entirely.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Had eluded' = past. The discovery has already happened → past tense main verb. B (overturned) is correct.

Text: 'The senator's proposal, which [___] controversial from the start, gained unexpected support after the independent analysis was released.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Which' refers to 'proposal' (singular, past context) → 'was.' C is correct.

Passage: 'Bioluminescence — the ability of living organisms to produce light — serves multiple evolutionary purposes. It can attract prey, deter predators, or facilitate communication between members of the same species.' Which choice best states the main idea?
Bioluminescence serves diverse evolutionary functions including predation, defense, and communication.
Light is important for marine animals.
C captures the full scope: diverse functions + three specific categories. A is too vague. B is subjective. D is too general. C is correct.

Text: 'The framework requires that all participating institutions [___] annual reports detailing their sustainability initiatives.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Requires that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (submit) is correct.

Text: 'Scientists [___] that the asteroid impact caused the mass extinction event 66 million years ago.'

Context: Overwhelming geological and biological evidence across multiple continents.

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Overwhelming evidence → definitive language. D (have established) is correct.

Text: 'The new regulations[___] neither codified in statute nor subject to standard administrative review procedures.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Which transition correctly completes: 'The study found no significant difference between the groups. [___], the researchers cautioned against drawing firm conclusions from such a small sample.'

'No significant difference' + 'cautioned against conclusions' — additional caution following a neutral result. C (nevertheless) is used here as an additional caution, but actually 'in addition' (B) might fit. However, 'nevertheless' fits better: the researchers found no difference BUT still cautioned = nuanced caution regardless of results. C is correct.

Text: 'By the time the investigation concluded, auditors [___] over 10,000 documents.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'By the time [past event]' → PAST PERFECT. C (had reviewed) is correct.

Text: 'If the board [___] the merger, the combined company would control nearly 40% of the market.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Hypothetical future condition → 'were to approve' (formal hypothetical). C is correct.

Passage: 'The philosopher argued that moral intuitions, however widely shared, should be treated as data points rather than as foundations. Our intuitions can be systematically biased, historically contingent, and subject to revision in light of argument and evidence.' As used in this text, 'contingent' most nearly means:
'Historically contingent' = dependent on particular historical circumstances (not universal or necessary). B is correct.

Text: 'Neither the pilot study nor the follow-up experiments [___] able to replicate the original findings.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Neither X nor Y': verb agrees with CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'experiments' (plural) → were. B is correct.
Which version correctly fixes the dangling modifier?
The conclusion was clear after analyzing all the data.
After analyzing all the data, the researchers reached a clear conclusion.
Both B and C are correct.
After analyzing all the data, the conclusion was clear.
B: researchers are the subject (they analyzed). C: restructured so 'after analyzing' is not an opening dangling modifier. Both work. D is correct.

Text: 'The species [___] declining for decades before it was finally listed as endangered.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Before it was listed' → declining preceded listing → PAST PERFECT. C (had been) is correct.
The report reached one inescapable conclusion: the policy had failed.
The report reached one: inescapable conclusion the policy had failed.
The report reached one inescapable conclusion; the policy had failed.
The report reached one inescapable conclusion, the policy had failed.
Complete clause + colon introduces explanation. C is correct. A uses semicolon (works but colon is better for a single conclusion). B = comma splice. D misplaces the colon.

Text: 'The legislation [___] if the governor does not sign it before the session ends.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Real/possible condition ('if...does not sign') + present tense → future/present tense result. A (expires) is correct.
The committee reached a unanimous decision.
The team's performance has improved significantly this season.
Each of the team members have submitted their reports.
The company revised its quarterly projections.
B: 'Each' is SINGULAR → 'has submitted,' not 'have submitted.' B is the error.

Text: 'The court ruled that the defendant [___] the disclosure requirements under the existing statute.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Court ruling about a past event → SIMPLE PAST. B (violated) is correct.

Passage: 'Critics have argued that the film's slow pacing undermines its emotional impact. However, many viewers report that the deliberate tempo creates a meditative quality that allows them to fully inhabit the characters' experiences.' The word 'deliberate' most nearly means:
'Deliberate tempo' = intentionally chosen pace (positive connotation, contrasting with 'slow pacing' criticism). B is correct.

Text: 'The study, along with subsequent analyses by independent research groups, [___] that the intervention is both safe and effective.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Along with subsequent analyses' = intervening phrase. Subject = 'The study' (singular) → confirms. B is correct.
Which choice correctly uses a semicolon?
The findings were published, however; the peer review process took over a year.
The findings were published; the peer review process, however took over a year.
The findings were published; however the peer review process took over a year.
The findings were published; however, the peer review process took over a year.

Text: 'The researchers insisted that their methodology [___] sound, despite the controversy surrounding the conclusions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Insisted that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (be) is correct.
Which version is NOT correctly parallel?
The committee reviewed applications, conducted interviews, and made final decisions.
The study measured cognitive function, emotional wellbeing, and physical health.
She researched the topic, drafted the report, and presented the findings.
The policy aims to reduce waste, improve efficiency, and costs should be cut.
C mixes verbs (reduce, improve) with a clause (costs should be cut). Should be: 'reduce waste, improve efficiency, and cut costs.'

Text: 'The ambassador's remarks [___] interpreted as a concession by both domestic and international observers.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Passage: 'The transition from hunter-gatherer societies to agricultural communities fundamentally altered human biology. Dental records show a dramatic increase in cavities following the adoption of grain-based diets, indicating that the nutritional profile of early agricultural food was in some ways inferior to that of foraged foods.' Which inference is best supported?
Hunter-gatherers were healthier in every respect than agricultural communities.
The shift to agriculture had negative consequences for dental health, suggesting that agricultural diets were less healthy for teeth than foraged diets.
All modern health problems stem from the adoption of agriculture.
Agriculture was a mistake for human civilization.
B captures the specific supported inference: dental cavities increased + foraged foods were nutritionally superior for teeth. A, C, D all use absolute or overclaiming language. B is correct.

Text: 'The commission required that each proposal [___] evaluated by at least three independent reviewers.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Required that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive). C (be) is correct.
Which version contains a comma splice?
The project exceeded its budget, so the board demanded an explanation.
Although the project exceeded its budget, the board approved continued funding.
The project exceeded its budget, the board demanded an explanation.
The project exceeded its budget; the board demanded an explanation.
B: two independent clauses joined by a comma only — comma splice.

Text: 'Research [___] that early childhood education programs produce long-term improvements in graduation rates, earnings, and civic participation.'

Context: Extensive longitudinal studies tracking participants over 30 years.

Which choice correctly completes the text?
30-year longitudinal studies = strong evidence → 'demonstrates.' C is correct.

Text: '[___] by the sheer volume of data available, the research team developed a machine learning algorithm to assist with analysis.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Opening participial phrase: 'Overwhelmed by...data' — the team was overwhelmed. B (overwhelmed) is the past participial form. Subject = 'the research team' — correct.

Text: 'By next year, scientists at the institute [___] on the project for a full decade.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'By next year' + extended ongoing action → FUTURE PERFECT PROGRESSIVE. C (will have been working) is correct.

Text: 'The collection of essays, though individually uneven, [___] a unified argument for the importance of place in shaping identity.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Collection' = singular collective noun → 'makes.' B is correct.

Text: 'Each of the participants in the study [___] asked to complete three surveys over a period of eighteen months.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?

Passage: 'The so-called Great Oxygenation Event, which occurred approximately 2.4 billion years ago, fundamentally altered Earth's atmosphere when photosynthetic bacteria began producing oxygen in quantities that exceeded what existing processes could absorb.' As used in the text, 'exceeded' most nearly means:
'Exceeded what existing processes could absorb' = produced more than could be absorbed = went beyond. C is correct.

Text: 'The research suggests that if urban planners [___] more green space into city designs from the beginning, heat island effects could be substantially reduced.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
Hypothetical/possible future condition → 'were to integrate.' C is correct.

Text: 'The report's conclusions were [___]: funding had been misallocated, oversight had failed, and accountability mechanisms were inadequate.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
The list: misallocated funding, failed oversight, inadequate accountability = highly critical findings. 'Damning' = devastating to reputation. C is correct.

Text: 'The attorney general insisted that all relevant documents [___] produced before the hearing.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
'Insisted that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB (passive). C (be) is correct.

Which choice best states the main idea of this passage?

'The migration of gray whales spans 12,000 miles round trip — one of the longest known migrations of any mammal. They travel from Arctic feeding grounds to breeding lagoons in Baja California, guided by magnetic fields and coastal landmarks. The journey is timed precisely to take advantage of seasonal food availability.'
Baja California is an important habitat for gray whales.
Whales use magnetic fields to navigate.
Gray whales undertake one of the longest mammal migrations, navigating via multiple mechanisms and timing their journey to maximize food access.
